light-reveal.def: The product emerges from pure black as exposure rises, with a barely perceptible push-in, and the closing shot runs the same move in reverse.
light-reveal.why: The reveal comes from light alone, with no fade or cross-dissolve. The camera hole, flash, and edge reflections appear in sequence, and the different reflections of each material (silver, orange, deep blue) show up one by one during the fade-up. The opening and the closing use the same camera position, so the film starts and ends on the same frame.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Rim light on 0.0–0.4s; fade-up 0.4–1.6s (1.2s, 36 frames); hold with slow push 1.6–4.4s (2.8s, 84 frames). Cut at 4.4s to three colorways: each fades up over 1.5s (45 frames), 0.1s apart from the left, starting 4.55s; cut back to the single phone at 7.0s; fade-out in reverse 7.35–8.55s (1.2s, 36 frames), rim light off 8.55–8.9s; wordmark 8.78–9.58s, held to 11s
Easing
Fade-up and fade-out cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power2.inOut); rim light and the hold push use sine.inOut; multi-color fade-up cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); wordmark power2.out
Camera

Perspective, 24° fov. Single-phone shot: close-up on the camera bar from slightly above, distance 13 units, push-in during the hold scale 1.00→1.03, no depth of field. Three-color shot: straight-on at distance 47 units, push-in 1.00→1.015 linear over 4.4–7.0s
Subject

A 3D phone (Three.js) that never moves. Exposure runs from 3.5% to 100% on one power2.inOut curve applied per material in order: lens glass and optics 0–0.55 of the curve, flash 0.18–0.72, metal edges and camera bar 0.30–0.95, back glass 0.45–1.0. Three colorways, left to right: silver, orange, blue, 8.7 units apart
Style

Pure black background. Rim pass: one hard strip light high and behind on the right, grazing the top and right edges. Key pass: large soft box upper left plus a hard strip on the right. ACES tone mapping at exposure 1.25, bloom, 0.28 vignette, 0.022 film grain; wordmark in Inter 600 76px, #ecebe8, blur 6px→0
light-reveal.prompt: Build a product opening called Light Reveal. Pure black background, one phone in a close-up on its camera bar (24° fov, distance 13 units, from slightly above). Render two light passes and add them: a rim pass (one hard strip light high and behind on the right, grazing the top and right edges) that fades in over 0–0.4s, and a key pass (large soft box upper left plus a hard strip on the right) that starts at 3.5% and rises to 100% over 1.2 seconds (0.4–1.6s) with power2.inOut (cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)). Stage that one curve per material: the camera lenses first, then the flash, then the metal edges and camera bar, and the back glass last, with no fade or cross-dissolve. Hold for 2.8 seconds (1.6–4.4s) and push in slowly by 3% (scale 1.00→1.03, sine.inOut); the phone does not move. At 4.4s cut to a straight-on shot of three colorways (silver, orange, blue) 8.7 units apart; starting 4.55s each fades up over 1.5 seconds with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), 0.1 seconds after the previous one from the left, while the camera pushes in 1.5% linearly. At 7.0s cut back to the single phone and run the key light down in reverse over 1.2 seconds (7.35–8.55s), then turn the rim light off over 8.55–8.9s. The wordmark fades in over 8.78–9.58s (power2.out, blur 6px→0, y 8px→0) and holds to 11s. Use ACES tone mapping, bloom, a 0.28 vignette, 0.022 grain, and no depth of field. Build it with Three.js (MeshPhysicalMaterial, per-material envMapIntensity) driven by a seekable time function, with GSAP for the wordmark.

Slowly fades up from black
Three phone colors light up together
vs: rotate-to-lockup
Light Reveal keeps the subject still and changes only the light; Rotate to Lockup turns the object to a target angle.
x-ray-dissolve
X-ray Dissolve switches between an inner layer and an outer shell, while Light Reveal only adjusts exposure.

device-push-in-focus.def: A line-art 3D laptop turns upright while closed, opens, pushes in on the keyboard, then pans from key to key in step with the option selected in the UI beside it.
device-push-in-focus.why: The key highlight and the dropdown selection on the right happen on the same frame, so viewers link each key to its setting at a glance. A long telephoto lens flattens perspective, so the keys stay flat and readable after the push-in. The material is white with a 1.2px dark gray outline, and yellow is the only color in the frame.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Intro: laptop rises 0–0.5s, turns upright while closed 0.5–1.2s (0.7s, 21 frames), lid opens 1.2–1.75s (0.55s, 17 frames), push-in on keyboard 1.6–3.2s (1.6s, 48 frames). Then three key groups: ⌥+Space highlight 3.3s, press 3.8s, off 5.0s; pan 5.0–5.8s (0.8s, 24 frames), ⌘+⇧+K highlight 5.6s, press 6.0s, off 7.2s; pan 7.2–8.0s (0.8s), fn highlight 7.8s, press 8.2s
Easing
Push-in and every pan cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); yaw, lid opening and camera retarget easeInOutCubic; rise easeOutCubic; highlight fade 0.2s easeInOutCubic
Camera

Perspective camera, 22° fov telephoto, fixed viewing direction (0.62, 0.78, 0.9); yaw turns from 35° to 0°, the screen lid opens 0°→112°; the push-in dollies 150→60 units onto the ⌥+Space span, then pans to the ⌘+⇧+K span (dolly 70) and to fn (dolly 30)
Subject

Each key sinks 0.22 units in a 0.25s press (0.08s down, 0.17s easeOutBack return); highlighted keys go from white to yellow, pressed keys darken to #e5b92f; the pan target is the key group of the option just selected
Sync
The dropdown selects at 4.95s and 7.15s and the pan starts 0.05s later; key highlight lands 0.6s into the pan (5.6s, 7.8s), the press 0.4s after that (first group 0.5s)
Style
White material with gray outlines (#a9a9a9 body 2.2px, #b8b8b8 keys 1.8px at 2x pixel ratio), yellow accent #f6c83e (highlight #f6d45a); 3D on the left (760px), UI on the right
device-push-in-focus.prompt: Build an input-method onboarding demo called Device Push-in Focus. Split the page: 3D on the left (760px), UI on the right. The left side is a line-art 3D laptop with white material, gray outlines (2.2px body, 1.8px keys at 2x pixel ratio), accent color yellow #f6c83e, and a Three.js perspective camera with a 22° fov (telephoto) looking along a fixed direction (0.62, 0.78, 0.9). Sequence: the laptop rises in over 0.5s, turns yaw from 35° to 0° while closed over 0.7s, opens the screen lid from 0° to 112° over 0.55s (easeInOutCubic for both), then the camera pushes in on the keyboard over 1.6s (expo.out, dolly 150→60 units) and the keys for the current option light up in yellow (0.2s). After a 0.5s hold the key sinks 0.22 units and springs back (0.25s). When the dropdown on the right selects a new option, pan the camera to the matching key group over 0.8s (expo.out) starting right after the selection; the new keys highlight 0.6s into the pan and press 0.4s after that. Pan targets are ⌥+Space, then ⌘+⇧+K, then fn.
says: The camera moves across the laptop to the key for each option
The laptop closes, opens, then pushes in on the keyboard
Pick a setting and its key lights up
vs: macro-pull-out-reveal
Device Push-in Focus serves one UI choice after another, each pan finishing within 0.8s; Macro Pull-out Reveal is one long shot that ends by pulling out to the whole device.

macro-pull-out-reveal.def: The camera drifts slowly across a surface at extreme close range, then one pull-back reveals the whole device or page.
macro-pull-out-reveal.why: Viewers first learn the material and texture up close, then see where those details sit in the whole as the camera pulls out. The depth of field is very shallow with only one band in focus, so a flat UI reads like a physical object. The pull-out is fast at first and slow at the end, which lands steadily on the full device.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s. Three macro shots: chart 0–1.7s (51 frames), deployment row 1.7–3.3s (48 frames), primary button 3.3–4.8s (45 frames); pull-out 4.8–6.0s (1.2s, 36 frames); residual drift 6.0–8.4s; focus racks out and the wordmark comes in 7.9–8.75s, held to 10.5s
Easing

Macro drift linear; pull-out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); residual drift linear; the focus band re-centers after each cut with power2.out over 0.5s; wordmark opacity power2.out 0.5s, scale 1.06→1 and blur 10px→0 expo.out 0.8s
Camera

CSS 3D, perspective 2000px, window tilted rotateX 25–26° and rotateZ −3° to −4°. Macro scale 4.2x, 4.2x, 4.0x; pans of 75, 80 and 60 window px (315, 336, 240 screen px), about 8–11% of frame width per second. Pull-out scale 4.0x→1x, rotateX 25°→11°, ending with the window at 80% of frame width. Residual drift scale 1.00→1.03, rotateX 11°→9.5°, rotateY −1°→−4°
Subject

A 1536×880 dashboard window rebuilt in DOM/SVG; it never moves and only the camera does. The pull-out starts from the primary button the last macro shot ended on. A pixel-grid overlay is visible during the macro shots and fades out 4.8–5.15s
Style

Near-black background #050506, raking light from the upper left (radial gradient rgba(150,170,210,0.13) from the top-left corner plus a 118° sheen), shallow depth of field from four stacked copies at blur 0, 2.6, 6 and 11px under a tilted focus band (half-width 100–125px), grain at 7.5% opacity re-rolled every 3 frames, vignette to 62% black
macro-pull-out-reveal.prompt: Build a product shot called Macro Pull-out Reveal. Total length 10.5 seconds. Rebuild a dashboard window (1536×880) in DOM/SVG and tilt it in CSS 3D (perspective 2000px, rotateX 25°, rotateZ −3° to −4°) on a near-black #050506 background with a raking light from the upper left. For the first 4.8 seconds the camera makes three linear macro shots at scale 4.0–4.2x, panning about 8–11% of frame width per second: a chart curve (0–1.7s), a table row (1.7–3.3s) and the primary button (3.3–4.8s). Depth of field is very shallow: stack four copies of the scene at blur 0, 2.6, 6 and 11px, masked by a tilted focus band about 200–250px wide across the middle of the frame that re-centers with power2.out 0.5s after each cut; overlay a pixel grid and grain. From 4.8 to 6.0 seconds pull back with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), scale 4.0x to 1x, relaxing the tilt to rotateX 11° and widening the focus band to 560px, until the window fills about 80% of the frame. Then drift linearly for 2.4 seconds (scale 1.00→1.03). At 7.9–8.75 seconds rack the focus out of the window and bring in the wordmark (scale 1.06→1 and blur 10px→0 with expo.out over 0.8s), holding to 10.5 seconds. The subject does not move; only the camera does.
says: Starts very close on a detail, then pulls out to show the whole product
The camera slowly pulls back from a detail to the full picture
A close-up, then a sudden pull-out to the whole page
vs: auto-zoom
Auto Zoom serves a single UI action in 0.6–0.8s and then pulls back so the action can continue; Macro Pull-out Reveal ends on its pull-out.
device-push-in-focus
Device Push-in Focus pans to one key after another on a single device; Macro Pull-out Reveal tours one detail in a single shot, then pulls out once.

x-ray-dissolve.def: The internal structure and the outer shell cross-dissolve from the same camera position, then the camera pulls back to the whole device.
x-ray-dissolve.why: The internal parts and the shell dissolve in exact alignment, so viewers see where the chip sits inside the body. Orange bleeds in from the glow before it switches to the body, so color changes before shape and the transition has no hard jump. One camera position explains what is inside.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Macro shots: chip close-up 0–2.1s (fade in from black 0–0.7s), board and camera modules 2.1–4.3s. Dissolve shot 2.9s (87 frames): inner part drifts 4.3–5.5s (1.2s, 36 frames), accent tint 4.85–5.65s, shell fades in 5.5–6.0s (0.5s, 15 frames) while the inner layer drops to 30% over 5.5–5.8s, holds 0.2s, and reaches 0 at 6.18s; pull-back 6.0–7.2s (1.2s, 36 frames); wordmark 6.4–7.1s; settle 7.2–10.0s
Easing

Dissolve and tint power2.inOut (cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)); drift sine.out; pull-back expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) with a 4-frame zero-velocity run-up, nearly stopped for the last 0.4s; settle sine.inOut; wordmark power2.out
Camera

Perspective 24° fov. Macro shots oblique with a shallow depth of field. Dissolve shot is frontal and fixed from 5.5s; the drift before it moves about 2% of frame width per second, easing to rest. The pull-back scales 5x→1x with radial shutter blur (180°), ending with the body at 70% of frame height; the vignette tightens during the pull-back; settle push 1.00→1.025
Subject

Two layers composited at the same position: the inner part (chip) at weight 1→0.3→0, and the phone shell at 0→1; the accent tint is masked by a Gaussian around the chip, so it bleeds in from the chip's glow first and the brightest shell edges arrive before the body fills in
Style

Black background, cool white top light (spot #dde8ff, cool-white strip lights), inner part in gray metal, shell in the accent color (cosmic orange rgb(255,107,41)); ACES tone mapping at exposure 1.25, bloom, 0.022 grain, wordmark Inter 600 40px
x-ray-dissolve.prompt: Build a reveal of a product's internal structure called X-ray Dissolve. Black background, cool white top light, 24° fov, ACES tone mapping, bloom and light grain. Open with two oblique macro shots with a shallow depth of field: a chip close-up (0–2.1s, fading in from black over 0.7s) and the board with its camera modules (2.1–4.3s). Then cut to a frontal fixed camera on the chip: drift very slowly (about 2% of frame width per second, easing to rest) from 4.3 to 5.5s. From the same camera position, dissolve in the shell render at the same position: tint the chip's glow with the accent color (cosmic orange) over 4.85–5.65s, fade the shell in over 5.5–6.0s with power2.inOut (cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)), and take the inner layer from 100% to 30% over 5.5–5.8s, hold 30% for 0.2s, then to 0% by 6.18s. From 6.0s pull back for 1.2 seconds with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) with a 4-frame run-up from zero velocity, scale 5x to 1x, with radial shutter blur, until the whole device is 70% of frame height. The vignette radius tightens during the pull-back, and the product name fades in 6.4–7.1s (power2.out, blur 6px→0). Settle with a slow push of 2.5% until 10s. The two renders must be aligned exactly.
says: The chip shows through the body, then becomes the whole device
The parts inside slowly turn into the shell
Like an X-ray into the device, then a pull-back
vs: light-reveal
Light Reveal adjusts exposure; X-ray Dissolve switches between two images, the inner layer and the shell.
macro-pull-out-reveal
The first half of Macro Pull-out Reveal is continuous movement across one surface; X-ray Dissolve completes a layer dissolve before pulling back.

text-object-interleave.def: Text and object interleave in depth: type rises from behind the product, a device slots into a gap in a sentence, or a word passes through an object and comes out as another word.
text-object-interleave.why: The text sits one layer behind the product, and the product covers about 1/3 of the wordmark, which creates a front layer and a back layer. The sentence breaks in the middle and the device becomes part of it, so the eye travels from the left word through the screen to the right word. Translation is shown through occlusion: the word goes in as black source text and comes out as gradient-colored translation, with no arrows.
spec: Timing

Film 11s with hard cuts at 3.2s and 7.8s. Wordmark-rise scene 0–3.2s: product lights 0–1.15s, sinks while the wordmark rises 0.9–2.7s (1.8s, 54 frames). Pass-through scene 3.2–7.8s: source text slides in 1.0s (30 frames; 3.75–4.75s and 5.85–6.85s), translation emerges 0.4s (12 frames; 4.75–5.15s and 6.85–7.25s). Slot-in scene 7.8–11.0s: device drops in 8.55–9.05s (0.5s, 15 frames), light ring glows 9.05–9.65s (0.6s, 18 frames)
Easing

Wordmark rise, device drop, translation emerging and lockup cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); source text slide linear; product lighting power2.inOut; word lighting and ring glow power2.out and power2.inOut
Camera

Fixed perspective camera, 20° fov, distance 34 units, medium close-up. When the wordmark rises, the case sinks from top 350px to 515px (165px, about 15% of frame height) while the wordmark rises 255px; slow drift: case scale +2.5% in the first scene, earbud scale +2% in the second
Subject

Layer order: text at the back, 3D product in the middle, text in front. In the pass-through scene the translation is clipped to start at the earbud tip (x 1060px) and the source text is hidden past x 820px; in the slot-in scene the sentence splits into two groups with a 400px gap, one earbud wide, and the left words light first (8.05s), the right words second (8.3s)
Sync

The light ring turns on after both word groups have lit and the device has dropped in (9.05s); the translation emerges at the earbud's sound outlet (tip at 1060px, 580px) and its language label follows 0.12s later
Style

Black background in the first and last scene, light gray #f5f5f7 in the middle one; wordmark vertical gradient #ff5a0a → #ff7a26 → #ffb27a → #ffd2ad (Archivo Black 340px), translation gradient #4b2dff → #9b33ff → #ff2f8a (background-clip: text), sentence words #5e5e63 lighting to #f5f5f7
text-object-interleave.prompt: Build a front-and-back interleave of text and product called Text–Object Interleave as an 11-second film with three scenes and hard cuts at 3.2s and 7.8s. Use three layers: text at the back, your 3D product in the middle (fixed perspective camera, 20° fov, distance 34 units), text in front. Scene 1 (black stage): the case lights up (rim 0–0.45s, key 0.25–1.15s), then from 0.9 to 2.7s it sinks 165px (about 15% of frame height) with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) while a large wordmark with a vertical orange gradient (#ff5a0a to #ffd2ad) rises 255px from behind its top edge and is clipped at the bottom. Scene 2 (light gray #f5f5f7): an earbud close-up with its sound outlet fixed on screen; source text slides at constant speed (linear) for 1.0s into the earbud and is hidden, then 0.4s later the translation emerges from the outlet with expo.out in a purple-pink gradient (#4b2dff to #ff2f8a, background-clip: text); run two passes (3.75–5.15s and 5.85–7.25s). Scene 3 (black): a sentence split into two word groups with a 400px gap one earbud wide; the left words light first (8.05s), the right words 0.25s later; the earbud drops into the gap from above over 0.5s with expo.out (8.55–9.05s), then its light ring glows over 0.6s (9.05–9.65s) and the wordmark settles in with expo.out. Use layered HTML + GSAP over a Three.js canvas.
says: The text rises up from behind the product
A phone slides down between two pieces of text
The text passes through the earbuds and comes out in another language
vs: word-by-word-highlight
Word-by-Word Highlight controls reading pace on plain text; Text–Object Interleave puts text and object into an occlusion relationship.
dispense-line-up
Dispense Line-up has objects slide out of the main subject in turn, synced word by word with the caption; Text–Object Interleave emphasizes the front-and-back layering of text and object.

dispense-line-up.def: Accessories slide out of the main object one by one into a row while the caption appears word by word, then retract in mirror order.
dispense-line-up.why: The number of words in the caption matches the number of accessories one to one, and the forward and reverse runs are symmetric, so the move is reversible. Accessory sizes step down from large to small, which gives the row a sense of perspective. The row has no guide lines or labels.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s in three shots (A 0–3.9s, B 3.9–7.6s, lockup C 7.6–10.5s), with two dispense passes. Each pass: extend 0.9s (27 frames), hold 1.1s (33 frames), retract 0.9s (27 frames); pass 1 extends 0.5–1.4s and retracts 2.5–3.4s, pass 2 extends 4.3–5.2s and retracts 6.3–7.2s. Accessories start 0.15s apart (about 5 frames), each slide-out takes 0.3s (9 frames)
Easing
Slide-out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); the retract is the exact time mirror of the extend; camera push sine.inOut; wordmark and subtitle expo.out
Camera

Perspective, locked side view at 13° fov with lens shift so the dock sits left and the row centre-right (shots A and C); shot B is a three-quarter view from the left at 23° fov so the row recedes in depth; 3% push-in per shot (scale 1.00→1.03); motion blur from 14 sub-frames over a 180° shutter
Subject

5 power adapters (140W, 96W, 70W, 35W, 20W) leave the dock's right face to the right and form a row sized from large to small, 0.42 units apart; the smallest leaves first and travels furthest, the largest leaves last; on retract they re-enter in the mirrored order, from right to left
Sync

Each accessory that slides out adds one word to the caption 0.1s after it starts moving, which appears directly with no fade (5 words, 5 accessories); on retract, words are removed in reverse order at 0.15s intervals
Style

Light gray-white background #f4f4f6, matte white product (#f4f4f3, roughness 0.62), large soft overhead box plus broad front fill, soft contact shadows on an invisible floor; no tone mapping; dark gray type #1d1d1f (50px captions, 156px wordmark)
dispense-line-up.prompt: Build an accessory showcase called Dispense Line-up as a 10.5-second film. Light gray-white background (#f4f4f6) with a matte white charging dock in a locked side view (13° fov, lens shift so the dock sits left and the row centre-right). 5 power adapters (140W, 96W, 70W, 35W, 20W) slide out of the dock's right face to the right and form a row sized from large to small: the smallest leaves first and travels furthest, each next one starts 0.15 seconds later, each slide-out takes 0.3 seconds with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), 0.9 seconds in total. Each time one starts moving, the caption below gains one word 0.1 seconds later that appears directly with no fade; the word count matches the accessory count. After a 1.1 second hold, retract as the exact time mirror over 0.9 seconds: the accessories return from right to left into the dock while the caption deletes word by word in reverse. Run two passes (0.5s and 4.3s start) with a second caption, cutting to a three-quarter view from the left (23° fov) for the second one, then end on the side view with the wordmark fading in at 7.75s (expo.out, blur 10px→0). Push in 3% over every shot with sine.inOut. Soft overhead light, soft contact shadows, 14-sub-frame motion blur on moving parts. Drive the 3D from a time function so the retract is a mirror, and use GSAP only for the caption words and wordmark.

Text pops up word by word as they come out
Then they go back in one by one
vs: text-object-interleave
Text–Object Interleave is front-and-back occlusion between text and object; the caption in Dispense Line-up syncs only with the accessory count.
converge-to-mark
Converge to Mark gathers many elements into one icon; the retract in Dispense Line-up returns to the original subject and creates no new shape.

rotate-to-lockup.def: An object spins with a long ease-out and stops at the exact angle that forms the logo silhouette or the hero view of the product.
rotate-to-lockup.why: The last frame of the rotation is the logo, and the motion shows where the flat mark comes from in three dimensions. Rotation speed keeps dropping, so the last 0.8s is a slow approach to the target. The material uses only three gray tones with flat light, so the angle reads clearly.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Spin 0.2–2.7s (2.5s, 75 frames): 1.62 turns, about 1.5 of them in the first second; fade-in 0.2–0.42s; still hold 2.7–5.0s (2.3s, 69 frames). Hard cut at 5.0s to the fragment-assembly shot: three slabs fly in from 5.14s, 0.8s each (24 frames), staggered 0.08s; lockup 6.55–7.45s (0.9s, 27 frames); held to 10s
Easing

cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out, normalized to end exactly at 1), no overshoot; rotation angle runs 1.62 turns × (1 − eased progress), and a tilt quaternion slerps to identity on the same curve; fly-in and lockup expo.out; fade-in smoothstep
Camera

Fixed orthographic camera, object centered; the hexagon silhouette height grows 324px→432px (30%→40% of frame height) on the spin curve. In the second shot the assembled mark is 300px tall, then shrinks to 150px and steps left to make room for the wordmark
Subject

A cube cut into three stacked slabs (gap 0.05 of the edge) flips around a tilted view-space axis (0.62, 0.74, 0.26); the end pose is isometric (rotX 35.264°, rotY −45°) with a vertex pointing at the camera so the silhouette is a hexagon matching the logo. The slabs sit staggered along the view diagonal until the final angle lines them up; bevel and face gradient fade out as the stone stops. In the fragment shot the slabs enter from the lower left, right and top, rotating 1.35–1.5 rad and scaling 1.25–1.3x→1x
Style

Near-black background #0b0b0c, three flat gray tones for three faces (top #ecebe7, darkest #5c5b58, left in between), no highlights; 180° shutter motion blur by sub-frame accumulation; wordmark Inter 600, 103px, #ecebe7
rotate-to-lockup.prompt: Build a logo ending called Rotate to Lockup. Near-black background (#0b0b0c) and a fixed orthographic camera. A cube cut into three stacked slabs (gap 5% of the edge) fades in at the center over 0.2–0.42 seconds and flips around a tilted axis for 1.62 turns; use expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) over 2.5 seconds (0.2–2.7s), so about 1.5 turns happen in the first second and the speed drops gradually, while its hexagon silhouette grows from 30% to 40% of frame height (324px to 432px). On the last turn the stone lands in an isometric pose (rotX 35.264°, rotY −45°) with one vertex pointing at the camera, lined up exactly with your logo outline; the slabs stay staggered along the view diagonal until that final angle. Hold still for 2.3 seconds with no overshoot. Use three flat gray tones for the faces (#ecebe7 top, #5c5b58 darkest, left in between), no highlights, with bevel and gradient only while it moves, and 180° shutter motion blur. At 5.0s cut to the second shot: the three slabs fly in from outside the frame starting 5.14s, 0.8 seconds each with expo.out, staggered 0.08 seconds, rotating into place and scaling from 1.3x to 1x to form a 300px mark. At 6.55s the mark shrinks to 150px and steps left over 0.9 seconds (expo.out) while the wordmark is uncovered from behind it (clip edge riding the mark, x −36px→0). Hold to 10s. It spins and stops at just the right angle

Rotate to Lockup turns one object to a target angle; Converge to Mark gathers many elements and compresses them into one icon.

Outline to Solid goes from line to fill; in Rotate to Lockup the material stays the same and only the orientation changes.

outline-to-solid.def: A wireframe or light-drawn outline appears first, then fills into a solid shape or material.
outline-to-solid.why: The shape comes before the material, so the first thing viewers remember is the silhouette. The light stays the only light source, and when the solid appears its highlight sits where the light comes from. The wireframe stage has very low opacity, so it does not compete with the solid that follows.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Product shot 0–8.2s: light point fades in 0.45–1.0s, outline draw 1.0–4.0s (3.0s, 90 frames), solid body fades in 3.3–4.8s (1.5s, 45 frames, overlapping the last 0.7s of the draw), wide highlight 3.8–5.3s (peaks 0.5s, 15 frames, after the body), outline fades to 14% 4.6–5.7s, LED 5.5–6.1s, still, then push 6.3–8.2s. Short logo version 8.2–11.0s (2.8s): wireframe 8.22–8.62s (0.4s) + fill wipe 8.66–9.26s (0.6s)
Easing

Outline draw cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power2.inOut: slow, then fast, then slow); body and highlight fade in on the same curve; light point and outline fade sine.inOut; push power2.in; the fill wipe uses power2.inOut
Camera
Perspective, 18° fov, fixed camera; still until 6.3s (1.0s after the highlight peak), then a slow push-in of 5% (scale 1.00→1.05) to 8.2s
Subject

A light point starts at the top center and two heads extend symmetrically to both sides, drawing the full outline down to the bottom center; line about 1.5px (tube radius 0.0105 units) with bloom and a halo on the heads; the solid body fades in inside the outline, and the brightest wide highlight (a separate light pass) comes last
Style

Pure black background, cool white line (rgb(214,235,255)), ACES tone mapping at exposure 1.2, bloom, 0.016 grain; the logo version uses a white background with a gray wireframe (#b4b4b6, 1.5px), a black solid (#0b0b0c) wiping in from left to right, and construction lines at 10% opacity
outline-to-solid.prompt: Build a product opening called Outline to Solid. Pure black background, 18° fov fixed camera. A point of light fades in at the top center over 0.45–1.0 seconds, then from 1.0s two heads extend symmetrically to both sides, tracing the full outline of your product down to the bottom center, with line width about 1.5px and bloom plus a halo on the heads. The outline draw uses power2.inOut (cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)) and takes 3 seconds. When the outline is nearly closed (3.3s), the solid product fades in inside it over 1.5 seconds, and the wide highlight, a separate light pass from above, reaches full brightness 0.5 seconds after the body (3.8–5.3s). The outline fades to 14% over 4.6–5.7s and a small LED comes on at 5.5–6.1s. Then hold still until 6.3s and push in slowly by 5% (power2.in) until 8.2s. For a logo (a 2.8-second cut on white): fade in a gray wireframe and 10%-opacity construction lines over 0.4 seconds, then wipe in a black solid from left to right over 0.6 seconds with power2.inOut, fade the wireframe and construction lines out, and scale the lockup 1.00→1.03 across the cut.

converge-to-mark.def: At the end, multiple elements gather and compress into a single icon or logo, always centered in the frame.
converge-to-mark.why: A slow drift followed by a fast gather contrasts speeds and gives a clear end point. The shape loses detail step by step, from a concrete product to geometry to a brand mark, while its position stays at the center of the frame without jumping. When the ending uses the same technique as the opening, the film closes on itself.
spec: Timing

Film 10.6s. Workspace demo 0–6.2s; the pieces drift down from 5.0s (1.2–1.5s, about 4–5% of frame height); converge from 6.2s: each piece starts 0–0.55s after 6.2s and takes 0.65–0.95s (20–29 frames); chrome leaves 6.2–6.7s, wallpaper washes to white 6.4–7.4s; mark lands 7.32s and settles over 0.65s (20 frames); wordmark pulls out 8.05–9.3s, tagline 8.9–9.7s, held to 10.6s
Easing

Drift linear; converge position on cubic-bezier(0.32,0,0.67,0) (power3.in, faster as they get closer) for one axis and power2.in for the other, so paths curve; scale power2.in, rotation power1.in, opacity fade power1.in over the last 35%; mark landing back.out(2.1); wordmark and tagline cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out)
Camera

Fixed frame, target icon at the center (960, 540). Slow push 1.00→1.035 linear over 0–6.2s (x −14px, y −6px), back to 1.0 over 6.2–7.1s with power2.inOut; after landing the lockup pushes 1.00→1.04 linear over 3.0s from 7.6s
Subject

17 pieces drift down, then gather on the center: 4 windows, a timer, a notification, a picture-in-picture, a command palette, 2 collaborator cursors, and 7 dock icons; they scale to 0.07–0.4, rotate 6–30° and fade out in their last 35%; the dock's own Tessel icon travels at full scale and the 200px mark takes over from it at the same size, leaving only the mark
Style

Light base #f5f5f7 under a pastel wallpaper (peach, pink, blue, lilac) that washes to white; white windows with 12px radius and soft violet shadows; indigo accent #5b5bf0 (icon gradient #8a8cff → #3d31d6) with four white tiles and one amber tile; faint violet vignette

From 5.0s drift every piece down at constant speed (34px per second). At 6.2s the menu bar and dock background leave over 0.5s, the wallpaper washes to white over 1.0s, and every piece travels to the center of the frame (960, 540): each starts 0–0.55 seconds after 6.2s and takes 0.65–0.95 seconds, with power3.in on one axis and power2.in on the other, scaling to 0.07–0.4 (windows 0.07–0.09), rotating 6–30° and fading out over the last 35%. tilted-ui-with-depth-of-field.def: A UI plane tilted 10–15° and shot up close, with only the active row in focus and the rest blurred.
tilted-ui-with-depth-of-field.why: Tilt, shallow depth of field, and grain make the screen UI read as a physical object, and they match the color grade of the live-action shots before and after it. Only the row being typed in is in focus, so the eye has nothing to search for.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Panel slides in 0–1.0s (30 frames); camera pans linearly 0–8.0s; typing 1.4–3.2s (47 characters); results swap 3.3s, rows stagger 0.05s (0.5s each from 3.5s); highlight appears 4.4s and hops at 5.1s and 5.82s (0.22s, 7 frames each); select press 6.3s; answer streams 6.72–7.8s (7 lines, 0.18s apart); pull-back 8.0–8.9s (0.9s, 27 frames); wordmark 8.3–8.9s
Easing
Pan and backdrop drift linear; panel slide-in, row reveals, highlight hops, focus jumps and the pull-back cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); select press back.out(2)
Camera

CSS 3D, perspective 1200px; panel (760×500px) rotated rotateX 18°, rotateY −16°, rotateZ 5° at scale 2.3; camera close, panning slowly sideways (x 110→−150px) while a follow offset keeps the active line at about 40% of frame height; the in-focus band is 168px of panel height, about 36% of frame height, and the pull-back at 8.0s halves the tilt (9°, −8°, 2.5°), scales 2.3→1.5 and widens the band to the whole panel
Subject

The active row is sharp; two blurred copies of the same panel (blur 4px next to the band, 13px beyond it) cross-fade over 60px and 200px masks; typing at about 30ms per letter with 75ms per space, caret blinking on a 1s cycle; the highlight moves down two rows of the results, then the answer streams line by line
Sync

The focus band jumps to the same row as the highlight (0.22–0.35s expo.out) and follows each answer line (0.18s); the press (scale 0.98, then back.out(2)) and the tag turning orange #ff6a3d land on the same frame at 6.3s
Style

Near-black #070708 backdrop with five blurred white diagonal bands (−25°, opacity 0.07–0.14) drifting 288px (15% of frame width) over 9s; panel rgba(28,28,30,0.78), radius 14px, 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.10); grain at 8% opacity re-rolled every 3 frames; vignette to 45% black; orange accent #ff6a3d

The panel slides in over 1.0s with expo.out and the camera pans sideways at linear speed for 8 seconds. Only the active row is sharp: stack three copies of the panel (sharp, blur 4px, blur 13px) under masks that cross-fade over 60px and 200px, with an in-focus band of 168px of panel height (about 36% of the frame) that jumps to the active row with expo.out. Type a 47-character query at about 30ms per letter (75ms per space) from 1.4s with a cursor blinking every 1s; at 3.3s swap to the results, whose rows fade in staggered 0.05s; from 4.4s a highlight moves down two rows (0.22s hops), and at 6.3s the selection presses (scale 0.98 then back.out(2)) while its tag turns orange on the same frame; then stream a 7-line answer 0.18s per line. auto-zoom.def: The camera pushes to the target element in 0.4–0.8s, holds for one click or input, then pulls back to the full view.
auto-zoom.why: Each push-in serves exactly one action and pulls back as soon as the action is done, so viewers always know where they are on the full page. The ease is fast at first and slow at the end, so the camera lands crisply.
spec: Timing

Film 11s with two push–act–pull sequences. Push-in 0.6s (18 frames) at 1.1s and 5.0s; hold 2.35s and 2.75s; pull-back 0.7s (21 frames) at 4.05s and 8.35s. Cursor moves 0.5s (1.8–2.3s and 5.7–6.2s), drag 0.6s (2.55–3.15s), click 6.25s, typing 6.45–7.45s, Enter 7.65s; window leaves and the wordmark comes in 9.25–10.5s

Push and pull cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); cursor moves power2.inOut; press 0.08s power2.out, release 0.22s back.out; motion-blur filter ramps up with power1.out and fades with power1.in
Camera

Put the whole window in one container, scale 2x on both pushes, with the target element translated to frame center (960, 540) and transform-origin at the container's top-left corner; blur 3px on each push and 2px on each pull (0.12s up, 0.3s down); a slow whole-scene drift scale 1.00→1.035 over 9.2s
Subject

The camera arrives first, and the cursor starts moving 0.1s after the push completes. Action one: drag a calendar card to the next day (grab 2.4s, drop 3.2s). Action two: click an empty slot (6.25s, ripple), a draft card opens, a title is typed, Enter at 7.65s

The drop at 3.2s changes the card, side panel, menu-bar text, activity log and toast on the same frame; Enter at 7.65s swaps the panel and shows the toast on the same frame; each pull-back starts 0.7–0.85s after the action while the toast is still showing; every push is 0.6s and every pull 0.7s on the same easing

Only after the push completes (0.1s later) does the cursor move: grab a calendar card at 2.4s and drag it to the next day over 0.6s; on the drop frame (3.2s) the card, side panel, menu-bar text and a toast all change together. morph-relay.def: One element keeps morphing into the next, replacing cuts, so the whole sequence has no hard cut.
morph-relay.why: The element from the previous segment becomes the subject of the next, so there is always only one shape changing in the frame, with empty space around it. Shape, corner radius, and text color inversion happen on the same frame, so the morph reads as one continuous action.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Headline word groups rise 0.2–0.9s; title→line 1.1–1.3s (0.2s, 6 frames), line→capsule 1.3–1.6s (0.3s, 9 frames), capsule→input box 1.7–2.1s (0.4s, 12 frames); typing 2.4–3.95s, send 4.2s; input box→window 4.55–5.3s (0.75s), page blocks 5.0–5.95s; window shrinks into a card 7.0–7.8s (0.8s, 24 frames), 11 gallery cards 7.6–8.6s; closing line→pill 9.15–9.65s, held to 11s
Easing

Line expansion, input box and window growth cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power3.inOut); capsule thickening, page blocks, shrink into the card and the closing pill cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); send press back.out(1.7)
Camera
Camera basically fixed; slow linear push 1.00→1.03 over 6.2–7.0s, then 1.03→1.08 with a small pan (x −24px, y −14px) over 7.6–8.6s while the gallery appears; closing drift 1.00→1.025 over 9.6–11s
Subject

One black shape (#111111) changes width, height and corner radius together: 960×3 line, 960×96 capsule (radius 48), 920×88 input box (radius 44), 1440×820 window (radius 18, fill #f6f1e8), then a 0.26-scale gallery card among 11 others; the headline shrinks into the input as the placeholder, the avatar and buttons fade in 0.3s (1.8s), and page blocks rise 24px
Sync

The headline turns white on the frame after the capsule starts thickening (1.33s, 0.04s); the surrounding gallery stays hidden until the card is formed (cards appear from 7.6s); the window fill flips to cream within the first 0.3s of its growth
Style
Near-white soft-lit background (radial #ffffff → #e9e9e9) with a black shape; one subject throughout; gallery thumbnails use 11 different site styles; closing wordmark white on a 440×112 black pill

wireframe-re-layout.def: Content fades to wireframes, the wireframes re-flow into a new layout, then each cell fills with new content in turn.

showcase-wall.def: A full-screen wall of work cards drifts diagonally at constant speed while slowly scaling up, then accelerates into one card at the end.
showcase-wall.why: The number of cards shows that many people use the product. The cards all have different colors, so color blocks take turns passing through the center of the frame while drifting, and the push-in on one card at the end lands the eye on a specific piece of work.
spec: Timing
Drift 0–5.9s (177 frames); push-in 5.35–6.0s (about 20 frames); hold on the landed card 6.0–7.65s, with a template bar rising at 6.3s (0.7s); pull-back 7.65–8.65s (1.0s); lockup from 8.3s; film 11s

Camera

A 2400×1600px wall translates x:-440, y:-260 toward the upper left over 5.9s (about 75px per second, 3.9% of frame width), scale 1→1.15 about the frame center; the film opens from black over 0.5s (power1.out); the push-in fills the frame with one card while its borderRadius goes 10→0
Subject

Six masonry columns of website screenshot cards, 360px wide with a 22px gap, column tops staggered between −260 and −40px, five card heights (202.5, 225, 360, 450, 480px); each card is a miniature page with its own palette and typeface; the push-in target is a 202.5px-tall SaaS template page
Style

Dark #0b0b0c stage; cards with 10px radius, a mix of white, dark, orange, yellow, and purple site designs in many different typefaces; after the hold the wall dims under a dark radial overlay (0.9s) and a ring-and-planet mark with a 136px wordmark takes over

A card wall moving diagonally, then pushing in on one card
vs: auto-zoom
Auto Zoom serves one action and pulls back; Showcase Wall drifts at constant speed and ends with a one-way push-in and a cut.
pile-up-and-clear
Pile-up and Clear adds elements one at a time and then clears them; the cards in Showcase Wall fill the frame from the start and move as a whole.

card-flip-to-code.def: The preview card rotates 180° around the Y axis and its back face shows the code.
card-flip-to-code.why: Preview and code are the front and back of one card, which says they are the same thing. The surrounding interface stays completely still during the flip, so the motion happens on one element only.
spec: Timing

Per component: flip to code 0.8s (24 frames), hold about 1s, flip back 0.8s (24 frames). Pricing card 1.03–1.83s, back 2.88–3.68s (hold 1.05s); sign-in form 4.56–5.36s, back 6.26–7.06s (hold 0.9s); notification settings flips to code 7.71–8.51s and stays; component swaps are hard cuts at 3.88s and 7.03s; window leaves 9.4s (0.7s), wordmark 9.85s; film 11s
Easing
One cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power3.inOut) curve for each 180°; Preview/Code pill slides 0.2s expo.out; cursor press scale 0.86 over 0.06s, release 0.18s back.out(2)
Camera
Whole window in frame with a continuous slow push, scale 1→1.05 over 9.4s linear; 3D stage perspective 2400px, perspective-origin 820px 500px; edge-on the card shadow narrows to scaleX 0.04
Subject

A 940×680px component card turns rotateY 0→180° about its center; the second turn continues 180→360° in the same direction; the back face is rotateY(180deg), a dark code editor (#0d1117) with file tabs, an install command, and line-numbered TSX; the front is white with a dot grid
Sync

The cursor clicks the Preview/Code switch at 0.98s, the pill and labels change at 1.0s, and the flip starts at 1.03s; card shadow width and a black shading overlay (opacity up to 0.2) read the same eased angle each frame; window chrome, sidebar and header stay still; swapping component changes card, title, panel and sidebar row on one frame
Style
Light app window with a dark stage and deep shadow; shadcn-style components on the front; GitHub-dark syntax colors on the back; JetBrains Mono for code
card-flip-to-code.prompt: Build a preview-and-code switch called Card Flip to Code. Put a 940×680px component card in a light app window with perspective 2400px (origin 820px 500px). Clicking a Preview/Code segmented control (the pill slides over 0.2s with expo.out) starts a 0.8s rotateY from 0 to 180° about the card center with power3.inOut. The back face is rotateY(180deg), a dark code editor, and both faces use backface-visibility: hidden. The card shadow width (down to scaleX 0.04) and a black shading overlay (up to opacity 0.2) follow the same eased angle every frame. Window chrome stays still, the camera pushes scale 1 to 1.05 over 9.4s, and at 9.4s the window leaves and your wordmark lands.
says: The preview card flips over and the back is code
A flip that switches between preview and code
The card turns halfway to show the source
vs: morph-relay
Morph Relay turns one element into a different shape; Card Flip to Code shows two faces of the same card, and the shape does not change.
control-driven-change
In Control-Driven Change a control changes the page on the same frame; here the trigger and the result are on the same element.

control-driven-change.def: The frame a control (color picker, toggle, dial) lands, the page result changes on that same frame. It can be split-screen with the control on the left and the result on the right.
control-driven-change.why: Control state and page result are strictly on the same frame, so cause and effect need no narration. In split-screen the left is a dark control and the right is light content, so control and content are separated by brightness.
spec: Timing

Close-up 0–0.85s, pull-out 0.85–1.75s (0.9s); color-dot drags 1.9–2.3s (0.4s, 12 frames), 3.3–3.7s (0.4s) and 6.9–7.4s (0.5s, 15 frames); dark-mode knob slides 5.0–5.17s (5 frames), theme flips at 5.17s; Brand popover reopens 6.1s (0.2s); window leaves 8.6s (0.7s), wordmark 9.1s; film 11s
Easing

Drags cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power3.inOut), with dot and cursor sampled per frame from the same curve; free cursor moves expo.out in x and power2.out in y; press scale 0.86 over 0.06s, release back.out(2) 0.18s; dot grab scale 1.18; page changes are hard sets on the landing frame
Camera
Opens as a 2.6x close-up on the inspector and popover (slow push to 2.66x), pulls out over 0.9s with expo.out to the whole window at 1.3x, then pushes slowly 1.3→1.36x linear until 8.6s
Subject

A website editor: the cursor drags a dot across a 200×132px color field in the Brand popover, from indigo #6366f1 to emerald #10b981, orange #f97316, and violet #8b5cf6; the cursor drifts 5–6px off the dot's path mid-drag; a Dark mode switch flips the whole page theme at 5.17s
Sync

Style
Shadcn-style editor window, light (#ffffff with #09090b text) switching to dark (#09090b with #fafafa text); the page takes the dot's color as its accent

Flip a switch and the page changes right away
Adjust on the left and the page changes at the same time

Locked-Layout Reskin is driven by hard cuts in the edit, with no control in the frame; Control-Driven Change shows the control, and cause and effect are expressed by a same-frame change.

locked-layout-reskin.def: Layout positions stay locked while the color scheme and fonts hard-cut every 6–10 frames.
locked-layout-reskin.why: With the layout locked, the viewer's eye stays in one place and sees only what changes with each switch. Cuts land on the strong beats of the music, and the skins differ enough in color.
spec: Timing

Skin cuts: 4 at 16-frame spacing (0.53s) from 1.0s to 2.6s; title card 3.13–3.73s (18 frames); 10 cuts at 8-frame spacing (0.27s) 3.73–6.13s; 11 cuts at 6-frame spacing (0.2s) 6.4–8.4s, landing on one skin; Enter applies at 8.67s; wordmark cuts 9.4–9.7s; film 11s
Easing
No transition, a class swap with tl.set on a single frame; only the toast (expo.out 0.35s), cursor move and the final scale push animate
Camera
Fixed; the editor window is 1632×918px (85% of the frame) with position locked; scale 1→1.03 linear over 1s after landing (8.4–9.4s)
Subject

One page (a 1240×828px site canvas) re-skinned through eight theme classes: Mono white, Gazette beige serif, Neon dark purple with lime and monospace, Fern green serif, Block orange with condensed black type, Sorbet pink and lilac, Poster blue with condensed caps, Noir dark with gold serif; layout and elements never move
Sync

A theme-list panel highlights the active row, and an arrow-down key cap lights for 3 frames on every cut; the cursor picks the Gazette row at 0.87s and the first cut follows at 1.0s; the title card colors come from the skins on either side (#fff1f5 background, #ff5a1f text)
Style

Each skin changes background, text, accent, border and font through CSS variables; saturated solid fields (Block #ff5a1f, Poster #2340ff) alternate with quiet light and dark skins; type styles differ clearly between skins

Swap it through eight skins by changing a theme class on a single frame, each skin changing background, text, accent, border and typeface through CSS variables (white Mono, beige serif Gazette, dark Neon with lime and monospace, green Fern, orange Block with condensed black type, pink Sorbet, blue Poster, dark gold Noir). The layout stays put while the colors keep jumping
Quick switching between different themes
vs: control-driven-change
Control-Driven Change shows a control that changes the result on the same frame; Locked-Layout Reskin has no control and conveys customizability through edit rhythm.
focus-hop
Focus Hop moves a single highlight block; Locked-Layout Reskin changes the skin of the whole page.

multiplayer-cursors.def: Enlarged two-color named cursors move across a canvas, leave comments, and drag items to reorder.
multiplayer-cursors.why: Enlarged cursors become characters in the frame, and the interaction between two cursors stages collaboration. The comment bubble matches its cursor's color, so it maps to a person at a glance. The thumbnail grid provides density, and after the push-in only a small part of it is visible.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s; avatars pop at 0.35, 0.8, 1.2, 1.53, 1.8s (0.25s each, spacing 0.45→0.27s); Liam box-select 1.9–2.65s; Maya's bubble 2.5s (0.3s), typing 2.65–4.05s at 15 characters per second, Enter 4.2s; push-in 4.3–4.7s (0.4s, 12 frames); press 4.8s, drag 4.95–5.75s (0.8s), reflow shift 0.4s each, drop 5.85s; pull-back 6.15s (0.6s); Present click 7.55s; lockup 8.75s
Easing

Push-in expo.out with a 3px blur pulse; drag power2.inOut with a 12px arc in y; avatars back.out(2.2); bubble back.out(1.7); reflow expo.out 0.4s; press scale 0.86 over 0.08s, release back.out(1.7) 0.22s
Camera

Canvas content scrolls up 140px over 4.3s linear (about 3% of frame height per second) while the whole scene drifts scale 1→1.04 over 8.7s; at 4.3s push in 1.4x onto the slide, cursors counter-scale by 1/1.4 to keep their on-screen size; pull back at 6.15s
Subject

Cursors 46×56px (about 5% of frame height), one black #141414 (Liam Ortiz) and one magenta #d81283 (Maya Chen), each with a name tag; Liam box-selects three slides, Maya rests on a green slide and a same-color comment bubble types "Can we lead with this?", then she drags slide 12 two columns left to position 10 while slides 11 and 10 shift one column right; the slide numbers and left panel list update on the drop frame; Maya then clicks Present and the slide opens full screen
Sync

Enter changes the bubble header from "typing…" to "Just now" on one frame; push-in follows Enter by 0.1s; the drag starts 0.5s after the push-in begins; on the drop frame (5.85s) slide numbers and the panel order change together
Style
White window on a #fafafa canvas with a 33-slide pitch deck in neon green, yellow, orange, and dark green slides; cursors with a white outline and a soft shadow

Named colored cursors moving all over
Collaborative comments and drag-to-reorder
vs: control-driven-change
Control-Driven Change has a single control change the result; Multiplayer Cursors has several cursors acting in parallel on a canvas.
focus-hop
In Focus Hop the cursor only guides a highlight block; in Multiplayer Cursors the cursors are characters and carry out comments and drags.

focus-hop.def: A highlight block or focus frame hops one cell at a time with the cursor, and the frame can take the color of the icon inside it.
focus-hop.why: The highlight block is the strongest color in the frame and leads the eye cell by cell. The focus frame takes its color from what is inside, so the selection state and the content share one palette. The one-cell-per-stop rhythm turns each pause into a choice.
spec: Timing

Window enters 0–0.7s; shelf act: camera push 0.5–1.3s, frame fades in 1.1s, five slides at 1.4, 1.9, 2.4, 2.9, 3.4s (0.25s slide, 8 frames, then 0.25s hold), frame hides 3.95s; grid act: camera drop 3.8–4.6s, cursor arrives 4.2s, highlight hops from 4.7s with 0.22–0.34s dwell (7–10 frames) across 11 cells to 7.34s, click 7.84s, pull-back 8.09–8.89s (0.8s); end card 8.5s, frame hops at 9.05, 9.28, 9.5s; film 10.8s
Easing

Grid highlight hops are hard jumps (tl.set); shelf slide expo.out 0.25s with the frame color tweening power1.inOut; camera moves expo.out 0.8s; cursor moves power2.inOut 0.14–0.2s; click ripple 0.45s, frame scale 0.975 then back.out(2.4)
Camera

Cropped close-up at 2.1x on the shelf (drifting to 2.2x linear over 2.6s); drops to 2.0x on the grid, follows the cursor row horizontally at 40% of the cell offset, and sinks about 300px over 2.6s; pulls back to the full window at 8.09s
Subject

Dark app-store window; shelf of 10 app cards (156×162px, 172px pitch) slides left one card per step under a fixed focus frame on the third slot; grid of 12 extension cells (307×134px, 4 columns) where the highlight hops along a snake path (0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 6, 5, 4, 8, 9, 10) with the cursor following ±8px off center; the last cell's Install chip flips to Installed on the click frame
Sync

The frame's outline (2px) and fill (rgba(r,g,b,0.15), plus a 0 0 36px glow on the grid) take the main color of the icon inside it, tweening through the shelf slide and jumping with each grid hop; the cursor crosses a cell boundary at the midpoint of its move
Style
Near-black #08080a stage, #121215 sidebar, gradient app icons; focus frame color follows the icon, 15px corner radius; end card with a four-tile mark and a 76px wordmark
focus-hop.prompt: Show a selection process with a shot called Focus Hop. Open a dark app-store window and push into a horizontal shelf of app cards at 2.1x (expo.out, 0.8s), drifting to 2.2x. A focus frame (2px outline, 15% fill) stays fixed on the third slot and takes the main color of the icon inside it; every 0.5s the cards slide left one slot over 0.25s with expo.out while the frame color tweens to the next icon, five times. Then drop the camera to a 2.0x grid of extension cells, where a highlight hard-hops cell to cell along a snake path with no transition, dwelling 0.22 to 0.34s per cell and taking each icon's color, while the cursor follows with small offsets and the camera follows the row and sinks about 300px. Click the last cell's Install chip: the chip flips to Installed on the click frame, the frame squishes to 0.975 and settles with back.out(2.4). Pull back over 0.8s and close on a four-tile mark where the same frame hops across the tiles.

The selection frame changes color with the icon
Wherever the cursor goes, it lights up

dock-arrival.def: A magnified Dock opens a gap, a new icon grows into it with one small spark, and a cursor click opens the window.
dock-arrival.why: A familiar macOS Dock motion says "an app was installed" with no text needed. The radiating short lines appear only once and are very small, which marks the landing point without taking over the frame.
spec: Timing

Gap opens and icon grows 0.45–0.95s (0.5s, 15 frames); radiating strokes 0.95–1.30s (0.29s each, staggered 0.02s, about 9 frames); cursor appears 1.5s and moves 1.5–2.1s (0.6s, 18 frames); tooltip 2.2s; press dim 2.4s (0.1s, 3 frames); window opens at 2.5s over 0.55s; typing 3.45–4.84s; checkbox click 5.8s; window closes 7.4s (0.42s); icon lands 7.8s, wordmark unfolds 8.4s (1.2s); film 11s
Easing

Growth cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) (back.out(1.4)); cursor cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) (power3.inOut); window open cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); strokes draw power2.out and retract power2.in; window close power3.in; wordmark expo.out
Camera
Dock magnified 3.0x on a fixed point, pushing slowly to 3.06x until 2.5s; at the click, cut to a medium shot (1.0x, drifting to 1.012x) where the window opens from a small size at the center
Subject

A 13-slot macOS Dock (12 icons and a separator); the new icon's slot grows width 0→64px (gap 0→8px) while its icon goes scale 0.6→1 and fades in, and neighbors slide apart as the Dock re-centers; after it settles, four 2.1px strokes (at −96°, −62°, −30°, 2°) flick out of its upper right corner; the Dock magnifies icons 1.58x near the cursor; the opened window is a notes app with a checklist
Sync

The icon dims (opacity 0→0.32) on the press frame at 2.4s and the window opens 0.1s later at 2.5s; in the window a checklist row types a new item at 0.042s per character, and the click at 5.8s checks the box, updates the counter to "3 of 5" and the progress bar to 60% on one frame
Style

Light gray-white #efeff2 base with a soft orange, pink, and blue gradient wallpaper; frosted Dock plate (backdrop-filter: blur(24px)); gradient squircle icons; the end card is a large icon plus a wordmark and one-line tagline
dock-arrival.prompt: Show your app being installed with a shot called Dock Arrival. The frame is a macOS Dock magnified 3x on a fixed point with a very slow push to 3.06x. Starting at 0.45s, open a gap between two icons over 0.5s and grow your app icon in it (width 0 to 64px, gap 0 to 8px, scale 0.6 to 1, back.out(1.4)). After it settles, flick four 2.1px strokes out of its upper right corner, each drawing in 0.13s and retracting by 0.29s, staggered 0.02s. At 1.5s the cursor enters and moves to the icon over 0.6s with power3.inOut, the Dock magnifies icons 1.58x near it, and a tooltip appears. At 2.4s the icon dims over 0.1s, and at 2.5s cut to a medium shot where a notes window scales from 0.16 to 1 over 0.55s with expo.out. Type a new checklist item at 0.042s per character, click its checkbox at 5.8s and change the checkbox, counter and progress bar on the same frame. At 7.4s fold the window back to the center over 0.42s with power3.in, land a large icon with back.out(1.5), then slide it left while the wordmark unfolds with clip-path and blur 10px to 0 over 1.2s with expo.out.

The icon grows in with a little spark
Click the icon to open a window
vs: morph-relay
Morph Relay is one element changing shape continuously; Dock Arrival adds a new element to the Dock and then opens a window on click.
pile-up-and-clear

pile-up-and-clear.def: Tasks, tags, or events pile up one by one until the screen is full, then clear in one step to a single result state.
pile-up-and-clear.why: The number and position of elements draw the feeling of "more and more things to do", with red tags gradually surrounding the person. On clearing, the color changes from red to green and many tags become one, so the before-and-after contrast takes a single image swap.
spec: Timing

Window arrives 0–0.9s; 22 emails land from 0.9s with intervals shrinking 0.62→0.05s (last at 5.32s); 8 desktop notifications 2.75–5.1s; select-all key HUD 5.45s, selection 5.85s; clear in one frame at 6.45s; Inbox Zero holds 6.45–8.4s (about 1.95s, 58 frames); scene fades 8.4s (0.5s), mark 8.7s, wordmark 8.8s, tagline 9.1s; film 10.8s
Easing

Row arrival: list shift expo.out (duration min(0.36s, 1.6× the interval)) and row fade power2.out up to 0.14s; badge pulse scale 1.15→1 power2.out 0.1s; urgent rows flash red for 0.9s; notifications expo.out 0.22s (scale 1.08→1, x 30→0); the clear is a single-frame tl.set; Inbox Zero image scale 1.07→1 expo.out 1.8s
Camera
Fixed medium shot with a slow drift, scale 1→1.035 over 8.4s linear (origin 50% 12%); the window enters y 46→0, scale 0.965→1 over 0.9s expo.out
Subject

A mail app (Cobalt) with 4 existing messages; 22 new ones land at the top of the Inbox and push the list down 52px per row, while the Inbox badge and Important tab counter step 5→26; urgent rows flash red; 8 desktop notifications stack at the window edge (88px pitch); command-A selects all 26 rows, E marks them done: list, notifications, selection bar and badge disappear and a dusk-landscape Inbox Zero panel with a green check and a toast takes over
Sync

Each arrival and its counter step share one frame; the command-A key caps and the row selection land on the same frame (5.85s); the E key cap, the clear, the toast and the Inbox Zero panel land on the same frame (6.45s)
Style

Light mail UI on a desktop wallpaper; red Urgent chips (#fde4e4 background, #c62f34 text), green check #2fb36a, a deep blue-violet dusk gradient for the result; the end card is a blue app mark with a lowercase wordmark and a one-line tagline
pile-up-and-clear.prompt: Show your product wiping out chores with a shot called Pile-up and Clear. From 0.9s, 22 new emails land at the top of the Inbox one at a time, the interval shrinking from 0.62s to 0.05s (the last at 5.32s); each row slides the list down 52px with expo.out and fades in, the Inbox badge counts from 5 to 26 with a 1.15 to 1 scale pulse on every arrival, and urgent rows flash red for 0.9s. The schedule fills up cell by cell
Tags surround the person, then all disappear
vs: wireframe-re-layout

word-by-word-highlight.def: Words in a small centered line brighten from gray to white one at a time, and the text never moves.
word-by-word-highlight.why: The type is only 2.5% of frame height with over 90% empty space around it, so reading pace is controlled entirely by the word-by-word brightening. A slowly rotating product sits under each selling-point card, so the card always has something to look at. In the closing version, the frame where the last word of the subtitle appears lines up with the end frame of the lid-closing motion.
spec: Timing

One 37-word paragraph: words appear 0–5.92s, the last finishes lighting at 6.34s, hold until the hard cut at 8.3s (about 1.96s, 59 frames); wordmark card 8.3–11s: letters from 8.42s (0.07s apart), tagline 8.8s; film 11s
Easing

Each word is set to #666 and then runs linear to #fff over 0.42s (13 frames); words appear with no movement; product fades up from black over 0.7s (sine in-out); mark expo.out 1.4s (rotation −40→0, meridian rx 20→0.6)
Camera

Text card fixed in the top band; the product is a 3D laptop on a turntable at a constant −13° per second (68°→−40° by 8.3s) with a slow camera push of 2.5% (fov 19°, elevation 17°); the wordmark card drifts scale 1→1.04 over 2.7s
Subject

Gap after each word = 0.075 + 0.0125 × letters seconds (0.09–0.22s), plus 0.42s after a period and 0.22s after a comma; each word appears at 40% gray (#666) and the next appears while the previous is still brightening; the whole paragraph holds and then hard-cuts
Sync

Reading rhythm follows word length and punctuation; the paragraph stays still while the product turns beneath it; at 8.3s the hard cut lands the wordmark, where each letter repeats the same gray-to-white step
Style

Pure black #000 background; white Inter 500 at 33px (3.1% of frame height), 1000px wide, centered, line-height 1.42, text-wrap: balance; wordmark 124px weight 600 with a white disc mark; bloom and fine grain on the product
word-by-word-highlight.prompt: Build a selling-point title card called Word-by-Word Highlight. Pure black background; a 1000px-wide centered paragraph of white Inter 500 at 33px (about 3% of frame height, balanced wrap) sits in the top band, with a 3D product turning slowly below it. Words appear in order with no movement. Each word is set to 40% gray (#666) and brightens linearly to white over 0.42s, and the next word appears while the previous one is still brightening. The gap after each word is 0.075s plus 0.0125s per letter, with an extra 0.42s after a period and 0.22s after a comma, so a 37-word paragraph finishes at 6.34s. Hold it until 8.3s, then hard-cut to a wordmark card where each letter brightens from gray to white 0.07s apart and a tagline fades in over 0.5s. The product behind turns at a constant 13 degrees per second while the text stays still.
says: One sentence lighting up word by word on black
The words turn from gray to white one at a time
The subtitle fills in word by word with the action
vs: rhythmic-typing
Rhythmic Typing appends characters one at a time with a cursor; Word-by-Word Highlight brightens whole words in sequence, with no cursor.
scattered-spec-type
In Scattered Spec Type the words land at spread-out positions and appear with a hard cut; in Word-by-Word Highlight the words sit on one line.

rhythmic-typing.def: Monospace text is typed character by character with a cursor at uneven human speed, then deleted and retyped.
rhythmic-typing.why: The screen holds only a cursor and one line of small text, with a great deal of empty space. Typing pauses 0.3–0.5s between words like real keystrokes, and deleting is twice as fast as typing, which splits the product name and the launch status into two beats. The font is the same monospace used for the numbered labels in the product UI.
spec: Timing

Film 11s: first line typed 0.17–4.51s (typo 'bakcoff' 1.2–1.57s, five backspaces 2.1–2.27s, retype 2.47–2.77s); hold 0.7s; delete 32 characters 5.21–5.9s; check mark and '214 tests passing' 6.47–7.77s; hold 0.4s; delete 8.17–8.43s; wordmark typed 8.63–9.0s; green cursor and tagline 9.43s; hold to 11s
Easing

No tweening: each character is an opacity hard set (tl.set) on a fixed 33.6px monospace grid; the cursor is solid on every keystroke, then 0.5s on / 0.5s off in idle gaps; slow drift scale 1→1.04 linear
Camera
Fixed; the line is left-anchored at x 240px and grows to the right; the terminal line drifts scale 1→1.04 over 8.53s and the wordmark 1→1.035 over 2.47s (linear)
Subject

Typing gaps 0.04–0.11s (about 9–25 characters per second) with 0.3–0.5s pauses between words; backspace 0.04s per character for the typo, 0.022s for the whole line, 0.015s for the status line; a solid white block cursor (33.6×66px) follows the end of the text; a 15-name feature rail at 13% opacity scrolls up 380px behind the line
Sync

A muted label 'TALON 2.4 / AGENT' (28px) appears at 0.15s and clears at 8.15s; the rail fades in at 0.9s and out at 8.05s; at 9.43s the cursor turns green #3ddc97 on the same frame the tagline appears
Style
Near-black #09090c background; JetBrains Mono 56px (5.2% of frame height) in #f2f2f4, prompt prefix in muted #70707c, check mark in #3ddc97; wordmark 150px weight 500; soft vignette
rhythmic-typing.prompt: Build a terminal title card called Rhythmic Typing. Near-black background (#09090c) and one line of JetBrains Mono at 56px with a solid white block cursor following the end. Type '> add backoff to webhook retries' character by character with uneven gaps of 0.04 to 0.11s and 0.3 to 0.5s pauses between words, including a typo ('bakcoff') that you fix with five backspaces at 0.04s each. Hold 0.7s, delete the whole line at 0.022s per character, wait 0.5s, then type a green check mark and '214 tests passing', hold 0.4s, delete at 0.015s per character, and type the wordmark at 150px. The cursor is solid on every keystroke and blinks 0.5s on and 0.5s off during idle gaps. Characters are hard sets with no fade. Behind the line, a list of 15 feature names at 13% opacity scrolls up 380px, and at the end the cursor turns green as a tagline appears. The whole piece runs 11 seconds with a slow scale drift of 1 to 1.04.

Typed, deleted, then a new line typed
The cursor blinks and the typing speed keeps changing

Word-by-Word Highlight brightens words and never deletes; Rhythmic Typing appends characters and has a cursor and delete-and-retype.
prompt-carousel
Prompt Carousel happens inside an input box with several prompts scrolling vertically; Rhythmic Typing is a single line of text.

prompt-carousel.def: A line under the headline thickens into a pill, becomes an input box, and types a list of prompts that scroll vertically.
prompt-carousel.why: The input box grows out of the headline itself, with no cut. The prompts show one semi-transparent 20% gray row above and below, so it reads as a list of options, and the only motion in the frame is vertical.
spec: Timing

Film 11s: title words 0.15–0.7s (0.09s stagger, 0.4s each); line 0.85–1.05s; thicken 1.0–1.3s; widen 1.4–1.8s; app shell fades in 1.65–2.3s; first prompt typed 2.15–4.87s (41 characters); scrolls at 5.27, 6.12, 6.97s (0.3s each); send press 7.82s; pill closes 8.07–8.57s; wordmark 8.42s, tagline 8.57s
Easing

Words expo.out 0.4s; line power3.inOut 0.2s; thicken expo.out 0.3s; widen power3.inOut 0.4s; carousel scroll cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 0.3s (9 frames); send press scale 0.88 over 0.07s, then back.out(1.7) 0.25s
Camera
Fixed framing with a slow push of the whole stage, scale 1→1.05 over 9.2s from 1.8s (linear); the content moves vertically, 90px per scroll
Subject

"What should we build?" in four words (64px, weight 600) rises y 19→0 staggered 0.09s → a 3px black line spreads from the center to 860px (scaleX 0→1) → thickens into a 112px pill (radius 56px) with a soft shadow, and the headline flips white → the pill widens 860→1280px while the headline shrinks to 30px into the text slot, with an attach button, a model selector and a send button fading in → header, chips and recent projects appear → the first prompt types at about 15 characters per second (extra 0.07s after spaces, 0.1s after punctuation, seeded jitter) → the column scrolls up 90px per row three times (0.4s after typing, then every 0.85s), old rows turning light gray above the pill and the next prompt shown at 22% opacity below → send, shell fades, pill closes to 480×124px around a white mark and wordmark
Sync

The pill thickens as the headline flips white (1.03s); the headline is replaced by the typing row at 1.9s; each scroll sets the incoming row's text white on the same frame as the column moves; the send press runs 7.75–7.82s and the shell fades from 7.97s
Style
Pure white background; the black pill (#111111) is the only large dark area; Inter, prompts at 30px weight 500; ghost rows rgba(17,17,17,0.22); very light shadows
prompt-carousel.prompt: Build an opening called Prompt Carousel. Pure white background; a centered four-word title ("What should we build?", 64px) rises 19px and fades in, staggered 0.09s per word with expo.out over 0.4s. A thin black line spreads outward from the text's midline to 860px over 0.2s, thickens over 0.3s into a 112px black pill, and the text turns white on the same frame. The pill then widens to 1280px over 0.4s with power3.inOut while the headline shrinks to 30px into the text slot, and an attach button, a model selector and a send button fade in around it. After the headline clears, type the first prompt at about 15 characters per second with a cursor following the last character, with the next prompt visible in 22% gray below the box. Then the whole column scrolls up one 90px row with a 0.3 second expo.out, 0.4s after typing and again every 0.85s, three times, with the old row turning light gray above the pill. Finally press send (scale 0.88, then back.out(1.7)), fade the shell, and close the pill to 480×124px around your mark and wordmark. A slow scale push of 1 to 1.05 runs through the whole piece.

The prompts in the input box scroll up to the next one
That AI-product input-box typing intro

Rhythmic Typing is a single line typed and deleted in the center of the screen; Prompt Carousel's container is an input box with several prompts scrolling vertically.
