scattered-spec-type.def: A spec line is split into words placed far apart on uneven baselines, with a connector word stepping up letter by letter.
scattered-spec-type.why: Words are spread far apart on staggered baselines, so reading the spec sentence has pauses. Italics are used only on key words such as "faster" and "Introducing", and the type stays at about 3% of frame height so it does not compete with the main picture.
spec: Timing

Four sentences of 2.05s each starting at 0.1, 2.15, 4.2, 6.25s: words appear over the first 0.76–1.04s, then the sentence holds about 1.0–1.3s and hard-cuts; wordmark card 8.3–11s: letters scatter in 8.35–8.8s, settle at 8.96s over 0.55s, tagline 8.96s; film 11s
Easing

Words and letters appear with tl.set hard cuts (no fade); stair letters sit at x: i×24–26px, y: −i×28–30px, and two of the stair words collapse to one line with expo.out 0.4s; the scattered wordmark settles expo.out 0.55s
Camera

One 3D lens model (Three.js, fov 20°) re-framed for each sentence: lens offset x +640, −640, +560, −520px with scale 1.0, 1.15, 1.2, 1.1, tilt and a 4% scale growth plus a few pixels of drift inside each 2.05s group; scale 1.35 behind the wordmark with the background dimmed to 34% opacity
Subject

Four sentences with word starts 0.12–0.42s apart, each word placed by its left edge on its own baseline: 'Now with 48 megapixels', 'Constant f/1.8 aperture from 24–70mm', 'Up to 18 hours per charge', 'Weighs just 312 grams, lens included'; connector words ('with', 'from', 'per', 'just') appear letter by letter on an uneven beat as a staircase; numerals are 128px weight 300; the wordmark 'Quarry' appears as scattered letters offset up to ±150px
Sync
Each sentence swap, camera re-frame and background change land on the same frame (0.1, 2.15, 4.2, 6.25, 8.3s); the wordmark and tagline settle on the same frame at 8.96s
Style

Near-black #070708 radial background with a vignette; white #f5f5f7 Inter 66px, Playfair Display italic 74px, numerals 128px weight 300, one muted 40px line; red #ff4a2b dot in the tagline; set over a dark 3D product render
scattered-spec-type.prompt: Write four spec lines with a shot called Scattered Spec Type: 'Now with 48 megapixels', 'Constant f/1.8 aperture from 24–70mm', 'Up to 18 hours per charge' and 'Weighs just 312 grams, lens included', each shown for 2.05s over a dark 3D product render. Each word appears with a hard cut and no fade, 0.12 to 0.42 seconds apart, at positions spread across the frame on different baselines, in white Inter 66px with key words in Playfair italic 74px and numerals at 128px weight 300. Connector words ('with', 'from', 'per', 'just') appear letter by letter on an uneven beat and step upward, each letter 24 to 26px across and 28 to 30px up; settle some of them into one line with a 0.4 second expo.out. Re-frame the camera with a new lens offset, scale and tilt on every sentence, with a 4% growth inside each group, and hard-cut between sentences. At 8.3s, scatter the wordmark's letters up to 150px off their slots, settle them into one line with a 0.55 second expo.out, and fade in a tagline.
says: The spec text pops up word by word at different positions
The words are spread wide apart with ups and downs
Small spec text mixing roman and italic
vs: rhythmic-typing
In Rhythmic Typing the text is appended character by character on one fixed line; in Scattered Spec Type the words land at spread-out positions.
word-by-word-highlight
In Word-by-Word Highlight the words turn from gray to white on one line; in Scattered Spec Type the words appear with a hard cut at staggered positions.

mark-to-wordmark-unfold.def: A logo mark sits centered, then the wordmark unfolds from behind it or outward from its center, optionally with a scramble-then-lock effect.
mark-to-wordmark-unfold.why: The mark and the name are bound into one action: the wordmark is pulled out from behind the mark, or the mark stays put while the other letters grow around it. Scrambled characters appear only on the newly added position, and the other letters stay stable. The opening and the ending can use the same move, one in black and one in white.
spec: Timing

Film 9.4s: product window shot 0–3.6s (drift 0–2.6s, push 2.6–3.6s); mark hand-off 3.6s; accent half leans back 3.75–4.05s and returns 4.15–5.05s; mark moves left and the wordmark unfolds 4.15–5.45s (1.3s), letters from 4.2s at 0.08s stagger (1.25s each); tagline 6.3s (0.8s); slow push 3.6–9.4s
Easing

Unfold and push cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); the mark moves x 322→0 while a clip-path left edge slides 250px→−72px; letters go from blur 12px→0 and opacity 0→1 (0.4s power1.out); the accent half rotation 0→−20° with power2.out 0.3s, then back with back.out(2.2) 0.9s
Camera

Product window at an angle (perspective 1600px): rotationY 9°→5.5°, rotationX −5°→−3°, rotation −1.4°→−0.7°, scale 1.06→1.16 over 2.6s linear; then a 1.0s expo.out push to about 12.6x (328/26) with the tilt flattened to 0, centering the sidebar mark; the lockup then drifts scale 1→1.05 over 5.8s
Subject

Shot 1: an issue-tracker window (3 groups, 17 rows fading in with 0.022s stagger, headers 0.12s) with a selection highlight stepping at 1.15s and 1.95s and a 'link copied' toast 1.4–2.3s, whose workspace logo is a 26×16.5px mark. Shot 2: that mark at 328×208px (two quarter discs, ink and accent) slides left by 322px while the 4-letter wordmark (286px, weight 600) is revealed from behind it letter by letter
Sync

The window mark and the vector mark swap on the same frame (3.6s) at the same size and position; the clip edge follows the mark's right edge; letters start 0.05s after the mark begins moving; the UI fades over the first 0.4s of the push
Style
Warm light #efece4 background, ink #14130f wordmark, accent #ff4a1f on one half of the mark; tagline in 22px monospace with 0.26em tracking; soft vignette
mark-to-wordmark-unfold.prompt: Build a brand ending called Mark-to-Wordmark Unfold. Start on a product window (an issue list) tilted in 1600px perspective (rotationY 9 to 5.5 degrees, rotationX -5 to -3, scale 1.06 to 1.16 over 2.6s with linear ease), then push 1.0s with expo.out about 12.6x into the small logo mark in its sidebar while the tilt flattens and the UI fades, so the mark fills the frame at 328px on a warm light background (#efece4). Hand off to a vector mark of two quarter discs (ink and orange) on the same frame. The orange half leans back -20 degrees over 0.3s and returns with back.out(2.2). Then the mark slides left 322px over 1.3s with expo.out while the four-letter wordmark is revealed by a clip-path edge that follows the mark's right side, each letter sliding out from behind the mark 0.08 seconds apart and going from blur 12px to sharp over 1.25s. Fade in a monospace tagline at 6.3s, and keep a slow scale push from 1 to 1.05 through the hold.
says: The logo appears first, then the brand name grows out
The mark slides aside and the name pulls out from behind it
The name pops out letter by letter from the middle to both sides
vs: chromatic-stretch
Chromatic Stretch locally distorts the wordmark itself with RGB ghosting; Mark-to-Wordmark Unfold is about the order in which the mark and the wordmark appear.
foreground-wipe-flash
Foreground Wipe & Flash is a transition between scenes; Mark-to-Wordmark Unfold is often followed by a white flash.

chromatic-stretch.def: Some letters of a wordmark stretch horizontally with RGB ghosting, distort in steps, then snap back clean.
chromatic-stretch.why: The background and the type are black and white, and only the few distorted frames show a saturated separation into cyan, magenta, and yellow, so the color flashes and never stays. The distortion acts only on some letters and the rest stay clean, so the wordmark remains readable.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s (315 frames). Wordmark: entry distortion 0.1-0.4s, second 0.73-0.97s, third 1.3-1.53s, smear-out 2.4-2.73s. Headline 1 enters 2.8s (settled 3.1s), re-distorts 4.0-4.17s, smears out 4.87-5.13s. Headline 2 enters 5.2s, re-distorts 6.4-6.57s, smears out 7.27-7.53s. Closing wordmark enters 7.6s (settled 7.9s), distorts 8.13-8.4s, tagline fades up 8.42s over 0.6s and holds to 10.5s
Easing

Stepped, no tween between states: each state holds 2 frames (66ms), then the ghost strength drops to 0.3 for 1 frame and the line returns clean. The stretch amount decays across the steps (4.4x, 3.7x, 2.9x, 1.8x). The master timeline runs ease: "none"; the tagline uses expo.out
Camera
Fixed frame with a slow push on each block, scale 1 to 1.03 over its on-screen time
Subject

Each distortion picks one letter segment (2-8 characters) and stretches it horizontally up to 4.4x (smear-out reaches 16x), scales it 1.1-1.55x vertically, arcs the baseline up to 28px, and squeezes the rest of the line to 0.6-0.96x. The R, G and B channels are warped separately and offset by 2.2% of font size each (about 4.7px at 214px) with a 12px horizontal blur on R and B; added on black and subtracted from the background, the misaligned channels read as cyan, magenta and yellow. Smear-out shifts the block left up to 420px and trails 22 fading copies
Style

Background #f4f4f6, black ink. Wordmark Inter 500 and 300 at 214px, letter-spacing -0.034em; headlines Inter 600 at 104px with 34px supporting lines at 47% opacity. RGB color exists only on distorted frames; settled frames are pure black on light gray
chromatic-stretch.prompt: Build a wordmark opening called Chromatic Stretch, 10.5s at 30fps. Light gray background #f4f4f6, black Inter wordmark centered (500 for the name, 300 for the suffix, 214px, letter-spacing -0.034em); the source film uses Ember Pro. Distort one letter segment at a time in 2-frame steps with no tweening: stretch it horizontally from 4.4x down through 3.7x, 2.9x and 1.8x, enlarge it 1.1-1.55x vertically, arc the baseline up to 28px, and squeeze the rest of the line to 0.6-0.93x. Warp the R, G and B channels separately, offset each by 2.2% of font size with a 12px horizontal blur on R and B, add them on black and subtract from the background so the edges split into cyan, magenta and yellow; drop the split to 0.3 for 1 frame, then return clean. Run three distortions on the wordmark at 0.1s, 0.73s and 1.3s, then smear it out to the left at 2.4-2.73s (stretch up to 16x, shift up to 420px, 22 fading trail copies). Swap in two headline blocks (2.8s and 5.2s) using the same enter, one re-distort and smear-out pattern, then bring the wordmark back at 7.6s with one more distortion at 8.13s and fade a tagline up at 8.42s (0.6s, expo.out). Push each block in slowly from scale 1 to 1.03; color appears only on distorted frames.

The wordmark distorts a few times and then recovers
An RGB-split glitch effect on text
vs: mark-to-wordmark-unfold
Mark-to-Wordmark Unfold changes the order in which the wordmark appears; Chromatic Stretch locally distorts a wordmark that is already visible.
foreground-wipe-flash
Foreground Wipe & Flash is a scene transition; Chromatic Stretch happens on the wordmark itself.

glass-lens.def: A transparent glass disc, loupe, or control moves over content, magnifying and refracting what lies beneath, with dispersion at the edge.
glass-lens.why: Barrel distortion at the edge says "this is glass" more than the magnification inside the lens does. The transition tool is the material being introduced: on the frame where the camera pushes in until the glass fills the screen, the background flips from black to light gray-white, and the flip hides in the fully covered frame.
spec: Timing

Film 10.8s. Phone rises 0-0.9s. Tab-bar lens: pop 1.45s, slide Home to Library 1.6-2.3s, release 2.25s. Plus tap 3.0s, sheet up 3.1-3.75s. Caret loupe: pop 4.05s, hops 4.45-4.85s and 4.85-5.25s, drop 5.3s. Toggle: lens pop 5.45s, drag 5.55-5.95s, drop 6.0s. Create tap 6.05s, Now Playing up 6.2-6.95s. Scrubber knob: pop 7.2s, drag 7.35-8.45s. Camera push 8.1-8.8s, crossfade to the wordmark 8.6-8.95s, final lens slides 8.7-10.8s
Easing

Pop-in expo.out 0.28s, magnification ramp expo.out 0.3-0.35s, lens moves expo.out (0.7s tab bar, 0.4s per caret hop, 0.4s toggle, 1.1s scrubber), release power2.out 0.26s, camera moves expo.out 0.7-0.95s with two none holds; the final lens drifts none over 2.1s. The glass and the content copy under it move in the same tween, same ease, same duration
Camera

A scaled stage, not a moving lens: scale 1.06 to 1.09, then pushes to 1.75 on the tab bar (0.95s), 1.8 hold, 1.15 on the sheet (2.45s), 2.3 on the caret line (3.6s), 2.9 on the toggle (5.1s), 1.1 pull-back (6.0s), 2.2 on the scrubber (6.95s), and 6.0 into the knob (8.1s), each 0.7-0.95s expo.out, centered on the control about to get glass
Subject

Glass is a scaled copy of the same content clipped to a pill with saturate(1.2) contrast(1.03): tab bar 72x56 at 1.55x, caret loupe 132x58 at 1.7x, toggle 64x40 at 1.5x, scrubber knob 64x38 at 1.6x, final wordmark lens 440x262 at 1.28x. Each pops from scale 0.7-0.85 to 1.0-1.12; controls are solid at rest and turn to glass only while dragged
Sync

The glass and its content copy are offset in the same tween. On arrival (2.25s) the tab color, selection pill, screen swap and lens release happen on one frame. The toggle thumb, track color (green #34c759 at 5.65s) and lens move together; the scrubber knob, fill and the elapsed and remaining time (0:41 to 2:41, -3:02 to -1:02, 7 steps) follow the lens
Style

Light gray radial background (#f6f7f9 to #dddfe5) with a 12% edge vignette; dark phone body. Glass has a white top highlight, 1.2px conic-gradient rim (pink, amber, green, blue, violet), 3px pink left and blue right inner edge shadow, and a soft drop shadow. Final wordmark Inter 600, 250px, letter-spacing -0.05em, #101114
glass-lens.prompt: Build a product tour film called Glass Lens, 10.8s on a light gray radial background (#f6f7f9 to #dddfe5, 12% edge vignette) with a phone UI that stays solid at rest and shows glass only on the control being dragged. Glass is a scaled copy of the same content clipped to a pill, with saturate(1.2) contrast(1.03), a white top highlight, a 1.2px conic-gradient rim (pink, amber, green, blue, violet) and 3px pink and blue inner edge shadows; the glass and the content copy beneath it move in one tween with the same ease and duration. Pop each lens in over 0.28s with expo.out (scale 0.7-0.85 to 1.0-1.12) while magnification ramps over 0.3s: tab bar lens 1.55x slides from Home to Library over 0.7s at 1.6s and releases at 2.25s on the same frame the tab, screen and selection change; a 132x58 caret loupe at 1.7x pops at 4.05s and hops line to line, 0.4s expo.out each, at 4.45s and 4.85s; a 64x40 toggle lens at 1.5x drags the thumb 20px over 0.4s at 5.55s while the track turns #34c759; a 64x38 knob lens at 1.6x drags the scrubber for 1.1s at 7.35s with the elapsed and remaining times stepping 7 times. Animate the camera as a scaled stage that centers on each control before its lens appears (1.09, 1.75, 1.15, 2.3, 2.9, 1.1, 2.2, each 0.7-0.95s expo.out), push to 6.0x at 8.1s, crossfade over 0.35s at 8.6s to a 250px Inter 600 wordmark (#101114, letter-spacing -0.05em), and slide a 440x262 lens at 1.28x across it by 150px over 2.1s with ease: "none".
says: A clear glass piece magnifying the text under it
A magnifier following the cursor across a line of text
As a glass button slides by, the content under it is magnified and warped
vs: glass-droplet-split
Glass Droplet Split shows glass deforming and breaking apart; Glass Lens shows glass refracting and magnifying the content below it.
match-cut
Match Cut swaps in another object at the same anchor; Glass Lens flips the scene on the one frame where the lens fills the screen.

glass-droplet-split.def: A glass slab stretches into a droplet, its neck thins and breaks, leaving a round bead. A dispersive glass ring contracting inward is the sibling form.
glass-droplet-split.why: On an all-black background, a single highlight along the glass edge outlines the shape, with no fill and no shadow. The stretch and break follow surface tension, and the bead rebounds about 5% at the moment of separation; this bead becomes the prototype of the button that follows. The ring version separates the spikes outside the ring from the quiet text inside it, so the graphic itself explains noise reduction.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Slab arc slide 0-1.2s, stand up and stretch 1.2-2.2s, neck thins 2.12-2.41s and breaks at 2.41s, bead hovers 2.45-3.45s, bead opens into a ring 3.45-3.75s, ring contracts 3.75-4.55s, settling jitter 4.55-6.75s, ring gathers into a logo bead 6.75-7.35s, wordmark 7.42s and subline 7.8s hold to 10s
Easing

Stretch and rotate cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); break rebound cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) over 0.5s; ring contraction cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) over 0.8s; ring gather cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) over 0.6s; wordmark and subline expo.out (0.9s, 0.8s)
Camera

Perspective camera (15 degree field) arcs from 101.5 to 90 degrees at radius 1500 over 0-1.2s with ease 1-(1-t)^1.6 while pulling back 200 units, then holds fixed until a 3% push 7.35-10s with sine.inOut
Subject

A thin glass slab (thickness 0.085 of its width) slides along an arc and rotates upright from 54 degrees about its long axis and -68 degrees roll to 0, thickening to 0.5 and scaling 1 to 1.3. Its lower end stretches to a droplet (lower radius 150 to 270, tip down to -700), the neck thins from radius 18 to 1.6, then breaks at 2.41s with a flash; the lower body falls away and a bead (radius 150 shrinking to 70, about 54px below frame center) swells 5% and rebounds 8% vertically. At 3.45s the bead opens into a ring that contracts from radius 1000 to 350 with tube radius 120 to 34, jitters 5px at 5.5Hz and sprouts up to 18 spikes of 90-240px, then collapses into a 86px logo bead 310px left of center
Style

branching-growth.def: A single dot branches layer by layer into a network, slow at first and then faster, or splits in doubling beats until it fills the frame.
branching-growth.why: Going from one dot to thousands uses only black lines, black dots, and paper texture. Growth is slow at first and fast later, which turns scale into a visible rhythm. The big nodes and the small end dots differ greatly in size, so the layers read at a glance. The doubling version advances by doubling the count each beat, with no arrows or numbers.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Tree on paper 0.45-3.2s: layers 1-3 take 0.5s each (0.45-1.95s), layers 4-6 take 0.333s each (1.95-2.95s), layer 7 at 2.8-3.2s; camera pull-back 0.45-3.45s; six nodes turn green 2.9-3.4s; dive into one node 3.95-4.35s, then a 4-frame darken to the dark scene. Doubling beats at 4.48, 4.95, 5.5, 6.1, 6.7, 7.3, 7.9s (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 77 documents); slate at 8.4s with tagline at 8.7s, holding to 11s
Easing

Nodes pop with cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1); each line is drawn outward from its parent with 1-(1-p)^2.4 over 60% of the layer window, then its dot pops at 92% of the line; the pull-back interpolates log-scale (constant zoom rate); the dive eases scale with t^3 and position with t^2; the document re-deal steps at 8fps; slate letters expo.out 0.4s
Camera

Starts at scale 2.0 with the root low in frame (330px bias) and pulls back over 0.45-3.45s until the network is about 80% of frame width, centered on the tree extents; dives into one green node over 3.95-4.35s until it fills a 44px radius; the dark scene is fixed; the slate pushes 1.035x over 2.6s

Radius 24, 17, 12, 8, 5.6, 3.6, 1.9; edge length 300, 235, 195, 150, 110, 80, 42 (times 0.88-1.12); line width 1.9 down to 1.0. iris-window-montage.def: A fixed circular window cuts rapidly between images, or revisits the same image, while its size jumps with the rhythm.
iris-window-montage.why: Dozens of images from completely different sources are unified into one series by the same circular frame, so the circle is what the viewer watches. During the fast cuts the eye remembers only the circle and the change of content. The scan-line version looks at the same network graph again through an oscilloscope view.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Fast cut 0-3.5s: 22 images at 6 frames (images 1-3), 5 frames (4-14), then 4 frames (15-22), i.e. 0.2s down to 0.133s; final image 3.5-3.7s; window opens 3.7-4.15s; push-in transition 4.15-4.65s. Scan window: expands 4.65-5.65s, hard jumps at 5.7, 6.1, 6.48s, green spread 6.58-8.33s with a jump at 7.43s, window closes to the mark at 8.38s, wordmark 8.74s, hold to 11s

Window size and image change are hard sets with no easing; per-image push ease: "none"; final window open expo.out 0.45s; push-in power3.in 0.5s, window fade power2.in 0.42s; scan window expands expo.out 1.0s; green nuclei pop scale 0.35 to 1 with expo.out 0.25s; window close expo.inOut 0.5s; wordmark expo.out 0.6s

Fixed. Inside the window each image starts at scale 0.6-1.0, random rotation up to +/-8 degrees and offset up to +/-40px, then drifts scale 1.02-1.05x and up to +/-1.5 degrees over its 4-6 frames. Scan-window scene: window 70px growing to 0.7H, jumps to 1.0H, 0.84H, 0.96H and 0.8H at 1.8x, 3.1x, 1.3x and 2.0x zoom, about 38% of 300 nuclei light green over 1.75s while a counter climbs to 312

map-pin-drop.why: Map, pin, and fragments use only one brand color plus deep blue and white, and the information is a single point and a single place name. The same pin-and-fragment burst carries on from the graphic world into real street view, connecting a customer from a dot on a map to a real storefront.

dot-matrix-glyph.def: A graphic is quantized onto a circular dot-matrix display, and every frame of its rotation or change snaps to the dot grid.
dot-matrix-glyph.why: Rotation is quantized onto a low-resolution dot matrix, so the motion jumps cell by cell and the edges are jagged, matching how real hardware displays work. Rotation speed drops from shot to shot, so the slowing down itself builds suspense, and alternating dot-matrix shots with expression shots deepens the wait.
spec: Timing

Film 11s, eight hard-cut shots. Wide rotation shots at 0-1.4s (rotation 0.8s), 1.85-3.55s (1.15s), 4.0-6.0s (1.6s), 6.4-8.8s (2.0s); close-ups of the crown 1.4-1.85s, 3.55-4.0s and 6.0-6.4s; each rotation covers 120 degrees and leaves the glyph still for 0.6, 0.55, 0.4 and 0.4s; captions at 2.0s and 4.12s; end card from 8.8s, tagline at 8.9s
Easing

Rotation cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (strong ease-out); crown click uses the same curve over 0.35s; dots turn on and off with a hard cut, no glow and no trail; camera pushes are linear inside each shot; captions expo.out 0.8s; scene fade-in 0.5s power2.out
Camera

Perspective camera (20 degree field) with a hard cut per shot: wide shots at zoom 1.0 (device body), 1.6, 1.95 and 1.7, each pushing linearly 2-16% inside the shot; close-ups of the crown and rim at zoom 4.2, 4.8 and 3.3 with depth of field; end card locked at zoom 1.98-2.0 on the screen

A 25x25 grid cropped to a circle of radius 12.3 cells (481 dots), dot diameter 60% of pitch. A vector glyph (arrow, hourglass, bell with badge, letter M) is rotated by angle each frame and every cell tests whether its rotated position falls inside the shape. Rotation runs from the final angle minus 120 degrees to 30 degrees for the arrow and 0 degrees for the others

line-boil.def: Hand-drawn outlines swap to a slightly different trace every few frames, and motion steps at a low frame rate with no tweening.
line-boil.why: Lines keep trembling slightly even when the picture is still, so the frame always seems to be moving while keeping the hand-drawn stroke. Low-frame-rate frame-by-frame animation reads differently from smooth tweened vector animation, and the action frame rate matches the boil frame rate.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Every state is a function of K = floor(t*7.5), so one new trace every 4 frames (0.133s) for the whole film. Scenes: chaos 0-2.67s (K 0-19), split inbox 2.67-5.87s (K 20-43), draft reply 5.87-7.87s (K 44-58), inbox zero 7.87-8.8s (K 59-65), wordmark 8.8-11s with the name at 8.93s
Easing

No tweening and no easing: position and shape jump per index. Flights are 3 positions on an arc, each held 4 frames (0.4s total); poses alternate every index; the whole canvas is redrawn from a clean white background each trace
Camera
Fixed; the scene is swapped on a white background with hard cuts at K 20, 44, 59 and 66
Subject

Each stroke is re-drawn every index with a smooth sine displacement of 1.05px amplitude plus a random offset of up to 0.65px per axis (about 1.7px), over a fixed 1.9px wobble. Open strokes get up to 3px of overshoot, fills sit up to 2.2px off the outline with marker streaks, and lettering uses 3 variants per letter. Character poses are mostly still; during an action the pose or position changes once per index (7.5fps)
Sync

All changes are hard cuts keyed to the same index: unread counter steps 48, 97, 131, 166, 212 at K 1, 4, 7, 10, 13; red labels appear at K 4, 7, 10, 13; one envelope launches per index from K 21 and lands 3 indices later; rules write in as each tray receives its first envelope; draft words arrive 3 per index; SENT, the cursor press and the reply flight follow in single-index steps
Style

Pure white background; ink #1c1a21 at 4.4px with pressure variation and a chisel or fine nib; flat color fills with darker marker streaks; green #16a35a for the brand and titles, red #e3352b for chaos labels, tray colors VIP #ffc417, TEAM #2f6bff, BILLING #ff7a1c, NEWS #f04e98

Each trace displaces every stroke with a smooth sine field of 1.05px amplitude plus a random per-stroke offset of up to 0.65px per axis, over a fixed 1.9px wobble; ink is #1c1a21 at 4.4px with pressure variation, tapered open ends with up to 3px overshoot, a chisel nib for titles and a fine nib for body text; fills are flat color offset up to 2.2px from the outline with darker marker streaks; lettering is single-stroke caps with 3 variants per letter. domino-wave.why: Each cube does only a simple flip, and the phase offset combines into a sense of forward motion. The material is a uniform matte dark gray, with faces told apart only by the top light. The slogan means moving forward, and the direction of the motion matches it.

From 6.2s it dives toward cube 7 and ends 1.28 units in front of its face as the roll eases to 0

Pass 1 turns each cube 90 degrees in the view plane with a 0.1 unit hop; pass 2 turns each 180 degrees with a 0.8 unit hop; pass 3 runs right to left, rolls each cube 90 degrees along the row with a 0.22 unit hop and brings the ring face toward the lens. Cube 7 carries an orange hex ring (#ff5a1f), the others a dark groove. A white extruded arrow with a trail sweeps above the row

The five slogan words (Every write lands in order.) fade in 0.1s apart from 2.78s, following the left-to-right sweep of pass 2; the arrow passes before it. The push into cube 7 ends in a white flash at 7.42s that resolves into the end card, where the mark and wordmark Basalt appear

Run three waves with cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1): pass 1 from 0.34s turns each cube 90 degrees in the view plane (0.6s, 0.10s offset, 0.1 unit hop); pass 2 from 2.5s turns each 180 degrees with a 0.8 unit hop (0.72s, 0.10s offset); pass 3 from 3.75s runs right to left and rolls each cube 90 degrees along the row (0.6s, 0.07s offset, 0.22 unit hop). Sweep a white extruded arrow with a 6 unit trail across the top of the row at 0.95-2.45s with power2.inOut, and write the slogan along the row, rotated -11 degrees, word by word 0.1s apart from 2.78s with expo.out 0.7s and an 8px blur, fading out at 5.9s. match-cut.def: One object is replaced by another at the same anchor point, so the viewer's gaze never moves.
match-cut.why: The new subject appears exactly where the eye already is, so the viewer never has to search the frame. The product stopping at the spot where it is worn ties object and person together without a visible cut.
spec: Timing

Film 10s. Hard cuts at 2.0, 3.0, 3.75, 4.4 and 5.05s. Scene 1 push-in 0-1.3s then drift to 2.0s; popover opens 2.0s; status swap 3.3s; badge lands 3.75s; mic swap 4.6s; scene 6 cards from 5.2s, cursor 6.25-6.8s, click swap 6.85s; product fades 7.4s; avatar to center 7.45-8.55s; wordmark 8.1s; hold to 10s
Easing

Cuts are hard (opacity flips in one frame, no cross-fade); scene 1 push-in expo.out 1.3s; every scene then drifts 3% (scene 6: 5%) with ease: "none"; popover expo.out 0.4s; badge scale 0.6 to 1 expo.out 0.35s; cards expo.out 0.5s, 0.16s stagger; cursor expo.out 0.55s; press scale 0.88 power2.out 0.08s; avatar to center expo.out 1.1s
Camera

Each scene is a UI sheet whose own avatar is scaled to exactly 112px and centered on the shared anchor (780, 450), so the face stays still while everything around it changes; only the opening wide shot scales (0.55x to 1x); end card holds the avatar at 1.45x drifting to 1.5x
Subject

One orange avatar (#e8734a, 112px, initials MC) fixed at the anchor through six app scenes: team chat, calendar invite, issue tracker, pull request review, video call, and the product Kite, where cards fade up and a cursor clicks Approve. In the end card the avatar moves 40px right and 90px down, scales to 1.45x, swaps its initials for a gem glyph and becomes the mark beside the wordmark
Sync

Every cut lands with the new avatar exactly at the old avatar's position and size; each in-scene change is a one-frame swap placed after the cut (reaction 1.15s, status 3.3s, mic 4.6s, Approve to Approved 6.85s)
Style

Backgrounds per scene: blue radial (#6d83c9 to #2e2f6b), white, #0b0c0d, white, #141416, warm dark radial (#3a2219 to #09090a); accent #e8734a; Inter UI text and JetBrains Mono metadata. Wordmark Inter 600 128px, letter-spacing -0.035em, #f4f4f5
match-cut.prompt: Build a transition called Match Cut, 10s. Anchor one orange avatar (#e8734a, 112px, initials MC) at the same center (780, 450) for the whole film, and build six app scenes as UI sheets, each scaled so its own avatar is exactly 112px at that anchor: a team chat on a blue radial background (0-2.0s), a calendar invite on white (2.0-3.0s), an issue tracker in near-black (3.0-3.75s), a pull request review on white (3.75-4.4s), a video call in dark gray (4.4-5.05s) and the product on a warm dark gradient (5.05-7.4s). Cut hard between scenes by flipping scene opacity on a single frame with no cross-fade. The opening wide shot pushes from 0.55x to 1x over 1.3s with expo.out, then every scene drifts 3% (scene 6: 5%) with ease: "none". Inside scenes, use one-frame swaps for state (status at 3.3s, mic at 4.6s, Approve to Approved at 6.85s) and small expo.out entrances (popover 0.4s, badge 0.35s, cards 0.5s with 0.16s stagger from 5.2s, a cursor in 0.55s at 6.25s). At 7.4s fade the product out over 0.45s, move the avatar 40px right and 90px down at 1.45x over 1.1s with expo.out, swap its initials for a gem glyph, set the wordmark in at 8.1s (0.7s expo.out, 128px Inter 600) and hold to 10s.

foreground-wipe-flash.def: A defocused foreground object sweeps across and covers the frame to cut scenes, or a central glow blows out to white before the next scene.
foreground-wipe-flash.why: The transition object comes straight from the current scene (a ball, a halo), so viewers see the transition as part of the camera movement. The whole film uses only these two transitions and very few hard cuts, which keeps continuity in a monochrome style; the switch point lands on a fully covered frame.
spec: Timing

Film 11s, four scenes: logs explorer 0-2.6s, parameter 2.6-5.1s, trace waterfall 5.1-7.4s, wordmark 7.4-11s. Wipe 1: ball drifts 0-2.4s, sweep 2.4-2.9s (7 frames in, 8 frames out), scene swap at 2.6s. Flash: halo rises 4.83-5.1s (8 frames), swap at 5.1s, white fades 5.1-5.4s (9 frames). Wipe 2: ball drifts to 7.2s, sweep 7.2-7.7s, swap at 7.4s
Easing

Wipe enters with expo.out over 7 frames (0.233s) and exits right with power2.in over 8 frames (0.267s); flash halo rises with ease: "none" over 8 frames and falls with power3.out (cubic-bezier(0.33,1,0.68,1)) over 9 frames; scene camera moves are ease: "none"
Camera

Scene 1: camera moves right (content x 70 to -60, scale 1.26 to 1.36 over 2.6s) with a 3D tilt easing rotationY 9 to 6 (perspective 1700px). Scene 2: slow push 1.0 to 1.05 over 2.5s. Scene 3: x 70 to -50, scale 1.42 to 1.5, tilt the other way (rotationY -10 to -6). Scene 4: 1.0 to 1.05 over 3.6s
Subject

A matte black ball (2800px at scale 0.42-0.45 waiting at the lower left, blur 54px, soft top-left highlight) sweeps across the foreground to the frame center scale 1, then leaves right at scale 1.08. The flash is a 5200px radial gradient halo (white core to 42%) from the frame center scaling 0.05 to 1.5, then a full white plate. Small blurred spheres (150px, 70px, 190px) sit in the lower-right foreground
Sync

The scene swap lands on the frame the ball is centered (frame 78 and frame 222) or the frame white is full (frame 153); the ball sweep is 15 frames and the flash 17 frames. The final wordmark scene opens with a white seed glow at 7.4s that fades as the mark sharpens
Style

Light scenes: gray studio (#d7d7d9 to #bdbdc0, soft highlight at 68% 36%, 26% edge vignette); dark scenes: radial #131315 to #060607; ball matte black #09090a shading to #5b5b61 highlight; flash pure white. Wordmark Inter 600 190px, letter-spacing -0.045em, #f4f4f5
foreground-wipe-flash.prompt: Build transitions between scenes called Foreground Wipe & Flash, 11s: a light gray studio scene (0-2.6s), a dark scene with a large number counting 412 to 38 (2.6-5.1s), a second light studio scene (5.1-7.4s) and a wordmark scene (7.4-11s). Each light scene already contains a large matte black ball (2800px, blur 54px, soft top-left highlight) waiting at the lower left at scale 0.42-0.45 and drifting slowly while the camera moves right with a 3D tilt. At 2.4s the ball sweeps to the frame center at scale 1 with expo.out in 7 frames and exits right to x 3700 at scale 1.08 with power2.in in 8 frames; swap the scene on frame 78 (2.6s) when the ball fills the frame, and the next scene is already in frame as the ball leaves. Between the dark scene and the second light scene use a flash instead: release a 5200px radial white halo from the frame center, scaling 0.05 to 1.5 linearly over 8 frames, set full white one frame before the swap at 5.1s, then fade the white plate over 9 frames with power3.out. Repeat the wipe at 7.2s with the swap on frame 222 (7.4s), then open the wordmark scene with a white seed glow that fades as the mark and wordmark slide into place over 1.3s with expo.out. Use only these transitions in the whole film.

confirmation-burst.def: On the frame of a tap, payment, or confirmation, lines, squares, and dots radiate from the contact point, or an icon pops with a bounce and an echo outline expands.
confirmation-burst.why: Graphics appear only on key action frames such as a tap or a successful payment, which marks the key moments of the product. The fragments share shapes and colors with the maps and feature cards used elsewhere in the film. The confirmation icon has thickness and highlights that contrast in material with the flat interface, and the expanding outline reuses the same shape.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Keypad taps at 1.0, 1.22, 1.44 and 1.66s; fragment burst on the Review tap at 2.65s (expand 0.3s, drift to 0.64s, fade 0.64-0.8s); review screen takes over at 3.0s; Pay tap at 5.1s, button disabled state 5.1-5.3s, icon pops at 5.45s (scale 0.6 to 1.1 in 0.28s, to 1.0 in 0.24s), outline ring 0.6s in parallel; phone leaves 8.0s; wordmark 8.45s
Easing

Fragments expand expo.out 0.3s, then drift linearly 12px over 0.5s and fade power1.in 0.16s; icon scale power3.out 0.6 to 1.1, then power2.inOut 1.1 to 1.0; outline scale power2.out 1 to 3 and opacity power2.in 0.6 to 0 over 0.6s; check stroke power2.out 0.24s; button disable power1.out 0.2s
Camera

Not fixed: slow push 1.18 to 1.215 until 1.9s, then an expo.out push to 1.7 anchored on the Review button (0.6s from 2.0s) so the burst fills the lower frame; pull-back to 1.42 at 3.0s (0.9s), drift to 1.5 by 5.25s, 1.3 at 5.53s (1.0s) drifting to 1.36. A 54px touch indicator travels to each target and presses (scale 0.78 in 0.06-0.07s, back in 0.14-0.16s)
Subject

Burst: 6 elements leave the tap point upward and sideways at angles -26, -78, -156, -128, -52 and -104 degrees: a white line with navy outline, a navy line, a blue line, a navy wavy line, a white dot and a blue square, travelling 96-120px (about 20% of frame height at camera scale 1.7). Icon: after the Pay button turns into a disabled Sending state with a spinner, a 132px scalloped blue seal with gradient, inner highlight and shadow and a white check stroke pops in with a same-shape outline expanding behind it
Sync

The burst and the button press (scale 0.965) share the tap frame at 2.65s and the review screen takes over 0.35s later; for the icon, the disabled state starts on the tap at 5.1s and the icon pops 0.35s later, with the same button turning into Done on that frame
Style

Navy backdrop #0b1b6a with blurred bank notification cards (fade out at 8.0s), white phone UI, brand blue #1e45d6 and fragments in navy #0b1b6a, blue #2a58ee and white; icon gradient #86a4ff to #1530b4; wordmark Inter 700 168px, letter-spacing -0.055em, white
